36/// @brief Where a widget is drawn, in its backend's own units (a cell on the terminal; `Theme.unitWidth` and
37/// `Theme.unitHeight` on Qt Quick), from the top left of the window or screen.
38struct WidgetBounds {
39 /// @brief The left edge.
40 double x = 0;
41 /// @brief The top edge.
42 double y = 0;
43 /// @brief The width.
44 double width = 0;
45 /// @brief The height.
46 double height = 0;
47};

49/// @brief How the conformance cases read and drive one backend under test.
50///
51/// The driving operations act as a user would, through the backend's own input path where it has one; each may run
52/// pending work before and after it. Reading operations report what the widget shows now.
53///
54/// Whether a handler can run after its widget was destroyed is observable only for a backend whose input can be
55/// delivered later than the driving call, such as a queued connection; a probe whose `click` delivers before it
56/// returns passes that case without exercising it.
57class ConformanceProbe {
58public:
59 ConformanceProbe() = default;
60 virtual ~ConformanceProbe() = default;
61 ConformanceProbe(ConformanceProbe const&) = delete;
62 ConformanceProbe& operator=(ConformanceProbe const&) = delete;
63 ConformanceProbe(ConformanceProbe&&) = delete;
64 ConformanceProbe& operator=(ConformanceProbe&&) = delete;
65
66 /// @brief The backend under test.
67 /// @return The backend every case mounts on.
68 virtual IViewBackend& backend() = 0;
69
70 /// @brief The runtime the cases' signals and mounts belong to.
71 /// @return The runtime, whose owner `settle` drives.
72 virtual reactive::Runtime& runtime() = 0;
73
74 /// @brief Runs posted flushes and pending native events until nothing is left.
75 virtual void settle() = 0;
76
77 /// @brief The text a widget shows: a Text's or TextInput's text, a Button's or Checkbox's label, and the label of
78 /// the option a Select marks.
79 /// @param widget The widget.
80 /// @return The text, UTF-8; empty for a Select that marks no option.
81 [[nodiscard]] virtual std::string textOf(Widget const& widget) = 0;
82
83 /// @brief The widget's own visibility flag, as its last `setVisible` left it.
84 ///
85 /// Only the widget's own flag counts: a hidden ancestor, a collapsed panel or a closed dialog around it does
86 /// not make this false. That is what `RecordingBackend` records, and it lets a case tell which Tabs page slot
87 /// the mount hid.
88 /// @param widget The widget.
89 /// @return True for a new widget; false once `setVisible(false)` reached it and until `setVisible(true)` does.
90 [[nodiscard]] virtual bool visibleOf(Widget const& widget) = 0;
91
92 /// @brief Whether a widget accepts input, by its own flag: a disabled ancestor does not make this false, which
93 /// is what `RecordingBackend` records.
94 /// @param widget The widget.
95 /// @return True for a new widget; false once `setEnabled(false)` reached it and until `setEnabled(true)` does.
96 [[nodiscard]] virtual bool enabledOf(Widget const& widget) = 0;
97
98 /// @brief How many children a container has.
99 /// @param container The container.
100 /// @return The count.
101 [[nodiscard]] virtual std::size_t childCount(ContainerWidget const& container) = 0;
102
103 /// @brief A container's child.
104 /// @param container The container.
105 /// @param index The position.
106 /// @return The child, or null past the end. A case drives it as it drives a root.
107 [[nodiscard]] virtual Widget* childAt(ContainerWidget const& container, std::size_t index) = 0;
108
109 /// @brief Activates a button as a user would.
110 /// @param widget The button.
111 virtual void click(Widget& widget) = 0;
112
113 /// @brief Replaces a text field's text as a user typing would: whatever the field held is cleared first (select
114 /// all, or delete), so it ends up holding exactly @p text. `onChange` may see intermediate texts.
115 /// @param widget The field.
116 /// @param text The text to end up with.
117 virtual void type(Widget& widget, std::string_view text) = 0;
118
119 /// @brief Drags one widget onto another as a user would.
120 /// @param source The dragged widget.
121 /// @param target The widget it is dropped on.
122 virtual void drag(Widget& source, Widget& target) = 0;
123
124 /// @brief Dismisses a dialog or drawer as a user would (Esc on the TUI), or a dismissible banner, or removes a
125 /// removable badge with its remove control.
126 /// @param dialog The dialog, drawer, banner or badge.
127 virtual void dismiss(Widget& dialog) = 0;
128
129 /// @brief Selects rows of a table as a user would, so that the user's selection is exactly these rows.
130 /// @param table The table.
131 /// @param rows Positions among the table's current rows, in the order the user picks them: at least one, and
132 /// one only for a `Single` table.
133 virtual void selectRows(Widget& table, std::vector<std::size_t> const& rows) = 0;
134
135 /// @brief Clicks a row of a table as a user would, with the modifiers @p click stands for: none, Ctrl, or Shift.
136 /// @param table The table.
137 /// @param row A position among the table's current rows.
138 /// @param click How the click is modified.
139 virtual void clickRow(Widget& table, std::size_t row, RowClick click) = 0;
140
141 /// @brief Clicks a column's header of a table as a user would.
142 /// @param table The table.
143 /// @param column The column's index among the table's columns.
144 virtual void clickHeader(Widget& table, std::size_t column) = 0;
145
146 /// @brief The rows a table shows as selected.
147 /// @param table The table.
148 /// @return Their positions among the table's current rows, ascending.
149 [[nodiscard]] virtual std::vector<std::size_t> selectedRows(Widget const& table) = 0;
150
151 /// @brief Moves a text field's cursor as a user would (the arrow keys, a click), without changing the text.
152 /// @param field The text field.
153 /// @param position A byte offset into the text it shows.
154 virtual void moveCursor(Widget& field, std::size_t position) = 0;
155
156 /// @brief Where a text field's cursor is.
157 /// @param field The text field.
158 /// @return A byte offset into the text it shows.
159 [[nodiscard]] virtual std::size_t cursorOf(Widget const& field) = 0;
160
161 /// @brief Presses a keyboard chord as a user would with focus on a widget.
162 /// @param focused The widget focus is on; the probe moves focus there first if it must.
163 /// @param chord The chord, as a document declares it, such as `"Ctrl+S"`.
164 virtual void press(Widget& focused, std::string_view chord) = 0;
165
166 /// @brief Whether a widget has keyboard focus.
167 /// @param widget The widget.
168 /// @return True when it is the widget that has focus.
169 [[nodiscard]] virtual bool hasFocus(Widget const& widget) = 0;
170
171 /// @brief Chooses a menu entry as a user would, opening each submenu on the path first.
172 /// @param menu The menu.
173 /// @param path The entry's index at each level, from the top.
174 virtual void chooseMenuEntry(Widget& menu, std::vector<std::size_t> const& path) = 0;
175
176 /// @brief Opens or closes a collapsible section with its own control, as a user would.
177 /// @param section The section.
178 /// @param open The state asked for.
179 virtual void expand(Widget& section, bool open) = 0;
180
181 /// @brief Drops files from the operating system onto a drop zone, as a user would.
182 /// @param zone The drop zone.
183 /// @param paths The files' paths, in the order dropped; not empty.
184 virtual void dropFiles(Widget& zone, std::vector<std::string> const& paths) = 0;
185
186 /// @brief What assistive technology reads as a widget's description: a field's messages and then its
187 /// description, joined by line feeds; an overlay's description. A probe that reads none keeps the
188 /// default, and the cases that read one fail on it.
189 /// @param widget The widget.
190 /// @return The description; `nullopt` when the probe reads none.
191 [[nodiscard]] virtual std::optional<std::string> descriptionOf(Widget const& widget) {
192 static_cast<void>(widget);
193 return std::nullopt;
194 }
195
196 /// @brief Where a widget is drawn, for the layout cases (`layoutConformanceCases`). A backend that lays nothing
197 /// out, such as `RecordingBackend`, answers none and runs only `conformanceCases`; a layout case run on
198 /// it fails.
199 /// @param widget The widget.
200 /// @return Its bounds, in the backend's own units; `nullopt` when the probe reads no geometry.
201 [[nodiscard]] virtual std::optional<WidgetBounds> boundsOf(Widget const& widget) {
202 static_cast<void>(widget);
203 return std::nullopt;
204 }
205
206 /// @brief Where a text's lines are drawn: the box around them, in the units `boundsOf` uses, from the top left of
207 /// the window or screen. For the layout cases that place a text within its own width.
208 /// @param widget The text.
209 /// @return The box; `nullopt` when the probe reads none.
210 [[nodiscard]] virtual std::optional<WidgetBounds> textExtentOf(Widget const& widget) {
211 static_cast<void>(widget);
212 return std::nullopt;
213 }
214};

216/// @brief One scripted case.
217struct ConformanceCase {
218 /// @brief What the case checks; unique among the cases.
219 std::string_view name;
220 /// @brief Runs the case on a fresh probe.
221 std::function<std::optional<std::string>(ConformanceProbe&)> run;
222};

224namespace detail {

226/// @brief Collects a case's checks and keeps the first failure, so a case reads top to bottom.
227class Checks {
228public:
229 /// @brief Checks that a text is what it should be.
230 /// @param what What is checked, for the message.
231 /// @param expected The text it should be.
232 /// @param actual The text it is.
233 void text(std::string_view what, std::string_view expected, std::string_view actual) {
234 if (expected != actual) {
235 fail(std::string{what} + ": expected '" + std::string{expected} + "', got '" + std::string{actual} + "'");
236 }
237 }
238
239 /// @brief Checks a condition.
240 /// @param holds The condition.
241 /// @param what The failure message when it does not hold.
242 void that(bool holds, std::string_view what) {
243 if (!holds) {
244 fail(std::string{what});
245 }
246 }
247
248 /// @brief The case's verdict.
249 /// @return `nullopt` when every check held, else the first failure.
250 [[nodiscard]] std::optional<std::string> result() const { return _failure; }
251
252private:
253 void fail(std::string message) {
254 if (!_failure.has_value()) {
255 _failure = std::move(message);
256 }
257 }
258
259 std::optional<std::string> _failure;
260};

262/// @brief A row of the ForEach and Table cases.
263struct Entry {
264 /// @brief The row's key.
265 std::int64_t id = 0;
266 /// @brief The text the row shows.
267 std::string label;
268
269 /// @brief Memberwise equality.
270 /// @return Whether both fields match.
271 bool operator==(Entry const&) const = default;
272};
273
274/// @brief A ForEach of Texts, one per entry, keyed by id.
275/// @param rows The entries; must outlive the node's mounts.
276/// @param builds Counts the row views built, when not null; must outlive the node's mounts.
277/// @return The node.
278[[nodiscard]] inline Node entryList(reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> const& rows, int* builds = nullptr) {
279 return ui::forEach<Entry>(
280 rows, [](Entry const& entry) { return Key{entry.id}; },
281 [builds](reactive::Signal<Entry> const& entry) {
282 if (builds != nullptr) {
283 ++*builds;
284 }
285 return ui::text({.text = [&entry] { return entry.get().label; }});
286 });
287}
288
289/// @brief A one-column Table of entries, keyed by id, whose cell is a Text of the label.
290/// @param rows The entries; must outlive the node's mounts.
291/// @param options Selection, activation and `Common`.
292/// @param sortable Whether the column is sortable.
293/// @return The node.
294[[nodiscard]] inline Node entryTable(reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> const& rows, TableOptions options,
295 bool sortable = false) {
296 return ui::table<Entry>(
297 {{.label = "Name", .sortable = sortable}}, [&rows] { return rows.get(); },
298 [](Entry const& entry) { return Key{entry.id}; },
299 [](reactive::Signal<Entry> const& entry) {
300 return std::vector<Node>{ui::text({.text = [&entry] { return entry.get().label; }})};
301 },
302 std::move(options));
303}

305/// @brief A widget as a container.
306/// @param widget The widget.
307/// @return It, or null when it is not a `ContainerWidget`.
308[[nodiscard]] inline ContainerWidget const* asContainer(Widget const& widget) {
309 return dynamic_cast<ContainerWidget const*>(&widget);
310}
311
312/// @brief The root widget of a mounted container node, as the container it is.
313///
314/// The root of a mounted Switch, Tabs, Column, ForEach or Dialog is the widget the backend's `createSlot`,
315/// `createTabs`, `createStack` or `createDialog` returned, and each of those is a `ContainerWidget` by its declared
316/// type, so the downcast cannot fail for any backend that compiles.
317/// @param view The mount, of a container node.
318/// @return The root widget as a container.
319[[nodiscard]] inline ContainerWidget const& rootContainer(Mounted const& view) {
320 // NOLINTNEXTLINE(cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-static-cast-downcast): a container by the factory's type, see above
321 return static_cast<ContainerWidget const&>(view.root());
322}
323
324/// @brief A child of a widget that should be a container.
325/// @param probe The backend under test.
326/// @param parent The widget; null, or a widget that is no container, has no children.
327/// @param index The position.
328/// @return The child, or null.
329[[nodiscard]] inline Widget* childOf(ConformanceProbe& probe, Widget const* parent, std::size_t index) {
330 ContainerWidget const* const container = parent == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*parent);
331 return container == nullptr ? nullptr : probe.childAt(*container, index);
332}
333
334/// @brief The texts of a container's children, joined by commas.
335/// @param probe The backend under test.
336/// @param container The container.
337/// @return For example `a,b,c`; a missing child reads `<null>`.
338[[nodiscard]] inline std::string childTexts(ConformanceProbe& probe, ContainerWidget const& container) {
339 std::string texts;
340 for (std::size_t i = 0; i < probe.childCount(container); ++i) {
341 if (i != 0) {
342 texts += ',';
343 }
344 Widget const* const child = probe.childAt(container, i);
345 texts += child == nullptr ? std::string{"<null>"} : probe.textOf(*child);
346 }
347 return texts;
348}
349
350/// @brief The texts of the rows an `entryTable` shows as selected, joined by commas.
351/// @param probe The backend under test.
352/// @param table The table.
353/// @return For example `a,c`; a row without a first cell reads `<null>`.
354[[nodiscard]] inline std::string selectedTexts(ConformanceProbe& probe, Widget const& table) {
355 std::string texts;
356 for (std::size_t const row : probe.selectedRows(table)) {
357 if (!texts.empty()) {
358 texts += ',';
359 }
360 Widget const* const cell = childOf(probe, childOf(probe, &table, row), 0);
361 texts += cell == nullptr ? std::string{"<null>"} : probe.textOf(*cell);
362 }
363 return texts;
364}
365
366/// @brief Keys as text, for a failure message.
367/// @param keys The keys.
368/// @return For example `1,"b"`.
369[[nodiscard]] inline std::string keyTexts(std::vector<Key> const& keys) {
370 std::string texts;
371 for (Key const& key : keys) {
372 if (!texts.empty()) {
373 texts += ',';
374 }
375 if (auto const* const number = std::get_if<std::int64_t>(&key); number != nullptr) {
376 texts += std::to_string(*number);
377 } else {
378 texts += '"' + std::get<std::string>(key) + '"';
379 }
380 }
381 return texts;
382}

384/// @brief Case: a constant Text shows its text.
385/// @param probe The backend under test.
386/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
387[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> textShowsItsText(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
388 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), ui::text({.text = "hello"})};
389 probe.settle();

395/// @brief Case: a bound Text follows its signal, once per batch, and not for an equal write.
396/// @param probe The backend under test.
397/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
398[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> boundTextUpdatesOncePerChange(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
399 reactive::Runtime& runtime = probe.runtime();
400 reactive::Signal<std::string> word{runtime, "one"};
401 int evaluations = 0;
402 Mounted const view{runtime, probe.backend(), ui::text({.text = [&word, &evaluations] {
403 ++evaluations;
404 return word.get();
405 }})};
406 probe.settle();
407 Checks checks;
408 checks.text("a bound Text", "one", probe.textOf(view.root()));
409 runtime.batch([&word] {
410 word.set("two");
411 word.set("three");
412 });
413 probe.settle();
414 checks.text("a bound Text after a batch of two writes", "three", probe.textOf(view.root()));
415 word.set("three");
416 probe.settle();
417 checks.that(evaluations == 2, "the binding ran " + std::to_string(evaluations) +
418 " times; expected once at mount and once for the batch");
419 return checks.result();
420}

422/// @brief Case: `visible` and `enabled` follow their bindings.
423/// @param probe The backend under test.
424/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
425[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> visibleAndEnabledFollowBindings(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
426 reactive::Signal<bool> shown{probe.runtime(), true};
427 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
428 ui::button({.label = "Go",
429 .common = {.visible = [&shown] { return shown.get(); },
430 .enabled = [&shown] { return shown.get(); }}})};
431 probe.settle();
432 Checks checks;
433 checks.that(probe.visibleOf(view.root()), "a Button bound visible=true is hidden");
434 checks.that(probe.enabledOf(view.root()), "a Button bound enabled=true is disabled");
435 shown.set(false);
436 probe.settle();
437 checks.that(!probe.visibleOf(view.root()), "a Button bound visible=false is shown");
438 checks.that(!probe.enabledOf(view.root()), "a Button bound enabled=false is enabled");
439 return checks.result();
440}

442/// @brief Case: a click runs the button's action once, and what it wrote reaches the screen.
443/// @param probe The backend under test.
444/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
445[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> clickReachesAction(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
446 reactive::Signal<int> clicks{probe.runtime(), 0};
447 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
448 ui::button({.label = [&clicks] { return "clicked " + std::to_string(clicks.get()); },
449 .onClick = [&clicks] { clicks.set(clicks.peek() + 1); }})};
450 probe.settle();
451 probe.click(view.root());
452 probe.settle();
453 Checks checks;
454 checks.that(clicks.peek() == 1, "one click ran the action " + std::to_string(clicks.peek()) + " times");
455 checks.text("the label bound to the click count", "clicked 1", probe.textOf(view.root()));
456 return checks.result();
457}

459/// @brief Case: typing reaches `onChange`; a value set by the application is shown and not reported back.
460/// @param probe The backend under test.
461/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
462[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> typingWithoutEcho(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
463 reactive::Signal<std::string> name{probe.runtime(), ""};
464 int changes = 0;
465 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
466 ui::textInput({.value = [&name] { return name.get(); },
467 .onChange =
468 [&name, &changes](std::string text) {
469 ++changes;
470 name.set(std::move(text));
471 }})};
472 probe.settle();
473 probe.type(view.root(), "abc");
474 probe.settle();
475 Checks checks;
476 checks.that(changes >= 1, "typing did not reach onChange");
477 checks.text("the value after typing", "abc", name.peek());
478 checks.text("the field after typing", "abc", probe.textOf(view.root()));
479 int const typed = changes;
480 name.set("xyz");
481 probe.settle();
482 checks.text("the field after the application set a value", "xyz", probe.textOf(view.root()));
483 checks.that(changes == typed, "a value set by the application was reported through onChange");
484 return checks.result();
485}

487/// @brief Case: a Switch shows the selected case, nothing for a key without one, and remounts on a change.
488/// @param probe The backend under test.
489/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
490[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> switchShowsSelectedCase(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
491 reactive::Signal<std::int64_t> which{probe.runtime(), 0};
492 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
493 ui::switchOf({.selector = [&which] { return Key{which.get()}; },
494 .cases = {{.key = Key{std::int64_t{0}}, .node = ui::text({.text = "zero"})},
495 {.key = Key{std::int64_t{1}}, .node = ui::text({.text = "one"})}}})};
496 probe.settle();
497 ContainerWidget const& slot = rootContainer(view);
498 Checks checks;
499 checks.text("the case for key 0", "zero", childTexts(probe, slot));
500 which.set(1);
501 probe.settle();
502 checks.text("the case for key 1", "one", childTexts(probe, slot));
503 which.set(7);
504 probe.settle();
505 checks.that(probe.childCount(slot) == 0, "a key with no case and no fallback still shows a child");
506 which.set(0);
507 probe.settle();
508 checks.text("the case for key 0 again", "zero", childTexts(probe, slot));
509 return checks.result();
510}

512/// @brief Case: Tabs mount a page on its first selection, keep it, and show only the selected one.
513/// @param probe The backend under test.
514/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
515[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> tabsMountPagesLazily(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
516 reactive::Signal<std::size_t> selected{probe.runtime(), 0};
517 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
518 ui::tabs({.tabs = {{.label = "A", .node = ui::text({.text = "first"})},
519 {.label = "B", .node = ui::text({.text = "second"})}},
520 .selected = [&selected] { return selected.get(); },
521 .onSelect = [&selected](std::size_t index) { selected.set(index); }})};
522 probe.settle();
523 ContainerWidget const& bar = rootContainer(view);
524 Checks checks;
525 checks.that(probe.childCount(bar) == 1, "Tabs mounted a page that was never selected");
526 selected.set(1);
527 probe.settle();
528 checks.that(probe.childCount(bar) == 2, "selecting a tab did not mount its page");
529 Widget const* const first = probe.childAt(bar, 0);
530 Widget const* const second = probe.childAt(bar, 1);
531 checks.that(first != nullptr && !probe.visibleOf(*first), "the unselected tab's page is shown");
532 checks.that(second != nullptr && probe.visibleOf(*second), "the selected tab's page is hidden");
533 selected.set(0);
534 probe.settle();
535 // Read again rather than through `first`: a backend that destroyed the page would leave that pointer dangling.
536 checks.that(probe.childCount(bar) == 2, "re-selecting a tab mounted its page again");
537 Widget const* const reselected = probe.childAt(bar, 0);
538 checks.that(reselected != nullptr && probe.visibleOf(*reselected), "the re-selected tab's page is hidden");
539 return checks.result();
540}

542/// @brief Case: relabelled tabs keep the highlighted tab and its page. With B highlighted and its page shown, a new
543/// caption for B leaves B highlighted under the new caption, and B's page the one visible.
544///
545/// The tab count stays the same, so a backend must replace the captions in place: one that rebuilds its tab buttons
546/// loses the highlight, and one that ignores a second `setTabs` keeps the old caption.
547/// @param probe The backend under test.
548/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
549[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> relabelledTabsKeepHighlight(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
550 reactive::Signal<std::size_t> selected{probe.runtime(), 0};
551 reactive::Signal<std::string> caption{probe.runtime(), "B"};
552 Mounted const view{
553 probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
554 ui::tabs({.tabs = {{.label = "A", .node = ui::text({.text = "first"})},
555 {.label = [&caption] { return caption.get(); }, .node = ui::text({.text = "second"})}},
556 .selected = [&selected] { return selected.get(); },
557 .onSelect = [&selected](std::size_t index) { selected.set(index); }})};
558 probe.settle();
559 selected.set(1);
560 probe.settle();
561 ContainerWidget const& bar = rootContainer(view);
562 Checks checks;
563 checks.text("the highlighted tab before the relabel", "B", probe.textOf(bar));
564 caption.set("B \u00b7 3");
565 probe.settle();
566 checks.text("the highlighted tab after the relabel", "B \u00b7 3", probe.textOf(bar));
567 checks.that(probe.childCount(bar) == 2, "a relabel mounted or dropped a page");
568 Widget const* const first = probe.childAt(bar, 0);
569 Widget const* const second = probe.childAt(bar, 1);
570 checks.that(first != nullptr && !probe.visibleOf(*first), "a relabel showed the page of a tab not highlighted");
571 checks.that(second != nullptr && probe.visibleOf(*second), "a relabel hid the highlighted tab's page");
572 return checks.result();
573}

575/// @brief Case: a ForEach updates a row whose key stays in place, keeping its widget and not building its view
576/// again.
577///
578/// The build count is the deciding check: a widget address alone cannot tell a kept widget from a new one that the
579/// allocator placed where the old one was.
580/// @param probe The backend under test.
581/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
582[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> forEachUpdatesInPlace(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
583 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> rows{probe.runtime(), {{.id = 1, .label = "a"}, {.id = 2, .label = "b"}}};
584 int builds = 0;
585 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), entryList(rows, &builds)};
586 probe.settle();
587 ContainerWidget const& list = rootContainer(view);
588 Widget const* const before = probe.childAt(list, 0);
589 rows.set({{.id = 1, .label = "a2"}, {.id = 2, .label = "b"}});
590 probe.settle();
591 Checks checks;
592 checks.that(builds == 2, "updating a kept row built its view again: " + std::to_string(builds) +
593 " row views built for two keys");
594 checks.that(probe.childAt(list, 0) == before, "updating a kept row replaced its widget");
595 checks.text("the rows after an update", "a2,b", childTexts(probe, list));
596 return checks.result();
597}

599/// @brief Case: a ForEach follows inserts, removals and reorders.
600/// @param probe The backend under test.
601/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
602[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> forEachInsertsRemovesReorders(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
603 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> rows{
604 probe.runtime(), {{.id = 1, .label = "a"}, {.id = 2, .label = "b"}, {.id = 3, .label = "c"}}};
605 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), entryList(rows)};
606 probe.settle();
607 ContainerWidget const& list = rootContainer(view);
608 Checks checks;
609 checks.text("the rows as mounted", "a,b,c", childTexts(probe, list));
610 rows.set({{.id = 3, .label = "c"}, {.id = 1, .label = "a"}});
611 probe.settle();
612 checks.text("the rows after removing b and moving c first", "c,a", childTexts(probe, list));
613 rows.set({{.id = 3, .label = "c"}, {.id = 4, .label = "d"}, {.id = 1, .label = "a"}});
614 probe.settle();
615 checks.text("the rows after inserting d in the middle", "c,d,a", childTexts(probe, list));
616 return checks.result();

619/// @brief Case: a widget moved among its siblings keeps its native state; here, the text a user typed into a field.
620/// @param probe The backend under test.
621/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
622[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> movedRowKeepsNativeState(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
623 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> rows{
624 probe.runtime(), {{.id = 1, .label = "a"}, {.id = 2, .label = "b"}, {.id = 3, .label = "c"}}};
625 // The field's text is the widget's own: no binding sets it after the mount, so only the user's typing does.
626 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
627 ui::forEach<Entry>(
628 rows, [](Entry const& entry) { return Key{entry.id}; },
629 [](reactive::Signal<Entry> const& entry) {
630 return ui::textInput({.placeholder = [&entry] { return entry.get().label; }});
631 })};
632 probe.settle();
633 ContainerWidget const& list = rootContainer(view);
634 Widget* const field = probe.childAt(list, 0);
635 if (field == nullptr) {
636 return "a ForEach of text fields shows no first field";
637 }
638 probe.type(*field, "edited");
639 probe.settle();
640 Checks checks;
641 checks.text("the fields after typing into the first", "edited,,", childTexts(probe, list));
642 rows.set({{.id = 2, .label = "b"}, {.id = 3, .label = "c"}, {.id = 1, .label = "a"}});
643 probe.settle();
644 checks.that(probe.childAt(list, 2) == field, "moving a row replaced its widget");
645 checks.text("the fields after moving the edited one last; moveChild must keep a widget's native state", ",,edited",
646 childTexts(probe, list));
647 return checks.result();
648}

650/// @brief Case: a Dialog holds its content only while it is open.

654 reactive::Signal<bool> open{probe.runtime(), false};

656 probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),

659 probe.settle();

662 checks.that(probe.childCount(dialog) == 0, "a closed Dialog holds content");
663 open.set(true);
664 probe.settle();
665 checks.text("an open Dialog's content", "inside", childTexts(probe, dialog));
666 open.set(false);

672/// @brief Case: a new dialog is closed, and a closed dialog takes no input, neither a dismissal nor a click on a
673/// child; an open one takes both.
674///
675/// Built through the backend directly: a mount opens or closes every dialog it makes, and mounts a dialog's content
676/// only while it is open, so neither a new dialog nor a closed one with children can be reached through it.
677/// @param probe The backend under test.
678/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
679[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> closedDialogTakesNoInput(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
680 int clicks = 0;
681 int dismissals = 0;
682 std::unique_ptr<DialogWidget> const dialog = probe.backend().createDialog(nullptr);
683 dialog->setTitle("Confirm");
684 dialog->setOnDismiss([&dismissals] { ++dismissals; });
685 std::unique_ptr<ButtonWidget> const button = probe.backend().createButton(dialog.get());
686 button->setLabel("OK");
687 button->setOnClick([&clicks] { ++clicks; });
688 probe.settle();
689 probe.click(*button);
690 probe.dismiss(*dialog);
691 probe.settle();
692 Checks checks;
693 checks.that(clicks == 0, "a click reached a button inside a new dialog; a new dialog is closed");
694 checks.that(dismissals == 0, "a new dialog was dismissed; a new dialog is closed");
695 dialog->setOpen(true);
696 probe.settle();
697 probe.click(*button);
698 probe.settle();
699 checks.that(clicks == 1,
700 "a click on a button inside an open dialog ran its action " + std::to_string(clicks) + " times");
701 probe.dismiss(*dialog);
702 probe.settle();
703 checks.that(dismissals == 1,
704 "dismissing an open dialog called onDismiss " + std::to_string(dismissals) + " times");
705 dialog->setOpen(false);
706 probe.settle();
707 probe.click(*button);
708 probe.dismiss(*dialog);
709 probe.settle();
710 checks.that(clicks == 1, "a click reached a button inside a closed dialog");
711 checks.that(dismissals == 1, "a closed dialog was dismissed");
712 return checks.result();
713}
714
715/// @brief Case: a widget inside a hidden, disabled or collapsed container takes no input — no click, edit, drag or
716/// row selection — and takes it again once the container is shown, enabled and expanded.
717/// @param probe The backend under test.
718/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
719[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> unreachableWidgetsTakeNoInput(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
720 reactive::Runtime& runtime = probe.runtime();
721 reactive::Signal<bool> hidden{runtime, false};
722 reactive::Signal<bool> disabled{runtime, false};
723 reactive::Signal<bool> collapsed{runtime, false};
724 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> const rows{runtime, {{.id = 1, .label = "r1"}, {.id = 2, .label = "r2"}}};
725 int clicks = 0;
726 int edits = 0;
727 int drops = 0;
728 int selections = 0;
729 // Every gate sits at least two levels above the widgets it gates, so a backend that consults only a widget's
730 // direct parent fails: an outer Column hides or disables, a Panel inside it collapses, and an inner Column
731 // holds the widgets.
732 Node const widgets = ui::column(
733 {.children = {ui::button({.label = "Go", .onClick = [&clicks] { ++clicks; }}),
734 ui::textInput({.onChange = [&edits](std::string const&) { ++edits; }}),
735 ui::text({.text = "card", .common = {.dragKey = std::optional<Key>{Key{std::int64_t{7}}}}}),
736 entryTable(rows, {.selectionMode = SelectionMode::Single,
737 .onSelectionChange = [&selections](std::vector<Key> const&, SelectionChange) {
738 ++selections;
739 }})}});
740 Mounted const gated{runtime, probe.backend(),
741 ui::column({.children = {ui::panel({.title = "Outer",
742 .child = widgets,
743 .collapsible = true,
744 .collapsed = [&collapsed] { return collapsed.get(); }})},
745 .common = {.visible = [&hidden] { return !hidden.get(); },
746 .enabled = [&disabled] { return !disabled.get(); }}})};
747 Mounted const target{runtime, probe.backend(),
748 ui::panel({.title = "Target", .common = {.onDrop = [&drops](Key const&) { ++drops; }}})};
749 probe.settle();
750 Widget const* const column = childOf(probe, childOf(probe, &gated.root(), 0), 0);
751 Widget* const button = childOf(probe, column, 0);
752 Widget* const field = childOf(probe, column, 1);
753 Widget* const card = childOf(probe, column, 2);
754 Widget* const table = childOf(probe, column, 3);
755 if (button == nullptr || field == nullptr || card == nullptr || table == nullptr) {
756 return "a Column in a Panel in a Column does not show the inner Column's four children";
757 }
758
759 struct Gate {
760 std::string_view name;
761 reactive::Signal<bool>* flag;
762 };
763 std::array<Gate, 3> const gates{{{.name = "hidden", .flag = &hidden},
764 {.name = "disabled", .flag = &disabled},
765 {.name = "collapsed", .flag = &collapsed}}};
766 std::size_t row = 1; // each round selects the row not selected yet, so a reachable table reports a change
767 std::string text = "a";
768 Checks checks;
769 for (Gate const& gate : gates) {
770 std::string const where = " inside a " + std::string{gate.name} + " container";
771 auto const act = [&] {
772 probe.click(*button);
773 probe.type(*field, text);
774 probe.drag(*card, target.root());
775 probe.selectRows(*table, {row});
776 probe.settle();
777 };
778 gate.flag->set(true);
779 probe.settle();
780 std::array<int, 4> const before{clicks, edits, drops, selections};
781 act();
782 checks.that(clicks == before.at(0), "a click reached a button" + where);
783 checks.that(edits == before.at(1), "typing reached a text field" + where);
784 checks.that(drops == before.at(2), "a widget" + where + " was dragged and dropped");
785 checks.that(selections == before.at(3), "a row selection reached a table" + where);
786 gate.flag->set(false);
787 probe.settle();
788 act();
789 std::string const again = " once its container was no longer " + std::string{gate.name};
790 checks.that(clicks == before.at(0) + 1, "a click did not reach a button" + again);
791 checks.that(edits > before.at(1), "typing did not reach a text field" + again);
792 checks.that(drops == before.at(2) + 1, "a drag did not deliver its key" + again);
793 checks.that(selections == before.at(3) + 1, "a row selection did not reach a table" + again);
794 row = 1 - row;
795 text += "b";
796 }
797 return checks.result();
798}
799
800/// @brief Case: a setter given the text a field already shows changes nothing; in particular the cursor stays.
801///
802/// Built through the backend directly, so the setter is called with the shown text on purpose: a mount sends no such
803/// call for an accepted edit, but a re-assertion of a transformed one, or another renderer, may.
804/// @param probe The backend under test.
805/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
806[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> unchangedTextKeepsCursor(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
807 std::unique_ptr<TextInputWidget> const field = probe.backend().createTextInput(nullptr, TextInputMode::SingleLine);
808 probe.settle();
809 probe.type(*field, "abc");
810 probe.moveCursor(*field, 1);
811 probe.settle();
812 Checks checks;
813 checks.that(probe.cursorOf(*field) == 1,
814 "moving the cursor to 1 left it at " + std::to_string(probe.cursorOf(*field)));
815 field->setText("abc");
816 probe.settle();
817 checks.text("the field after setText with the text it shows", "abc", probe.textOf(*field));
818 checks.that(probe.cursorOf(*field) == 1, "setText with the text the field shows moved the cursor from 1 to " +
819 std::to_string(probe.cursorOf(*field)));
820 return checks.result();
821}

823/// @brief Case: an edit the document refuses snaps back, and one it transforms shows the transform.
824/// @param probe The backend under test.
825/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
826[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> textInputIsControlled(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
827 reactive::Signal<std::string> name{probe.runtime(), "kept"};
828 bool refuse = true;
829 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
830 ui::textInput({.value = [&name] { return name.get(); },
831 .onChange =
832 [&name, &refuse](std::string text) {
833 if (!refuse) {
834 std::ranges::transform(text, text.begin(), [](char character) {
835 return character >= 'a' && character <= 'z'
836 ? static_cast<char>(character - 'a' + 'A')
837 : character;
838 });
839 name.set(std::move(text));
840 }
841 }})};
842 probe.settle();
843 Checks checks;
844 probe.type(view.root(), "typed");
845 probe.settle();
846 checks.text("the field after an edit the document refused", "kept", probe.textOf(view.root()));
847 refuse = false;
848 // A character past `z`, and a capital, are left as they are.
849 probe.type(view.root(), "ty~Ped");
850 probe.settle();
851 checks.text("the field after an edit the document upper-cased", "TY~PED", probe.textOf(view.root()));
852 checks.text("the value after an edit the document upper-cased", "TY~PED", name.peek());
853 return checks.result();
854}

856/// @brief Case: a dialog the user dismisses but the document keeps open is shown again, with its content.
857/// @param probe The backend under test.
858/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
859[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> refusedDismissalKeepsDialogOpen(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
860 reactive::Signal<bool> const open{probe.runtime(), true};
861 int dismissals = 0;
862 int clicks = 0;
863 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
864 ui::dialog({.open = [&open] { return open.get(); },
865 .title = "Confirm",
866 .child = ui::button({.label = "OK", .onClick = [&clicks] { ++clicks; }}),
867 .onDismiss = [&dismissals] { ++dismissals; }})};
868 probe.settle();
869 ContainerWidget const& dialog = rootContainer(view);
870 probe.dismiss(view.root());
871 probe.settle();

873 checks.that(dismissals == 1, "dismissing the dialog called onDismiss " + std::to_string(dismissals) + " times");
874 Widget* const button = probe.childAt(dialog, 0);
875 checks.that(button != nullptr, "a dialog kept open lost its content");
876 if (button != nullptr) {
877 probe.click(*button);
878 probe.settle();
879 }
880 checks.that(clicks == 1, "a click inside a dialog the document kept open ran its action " +
881 std::to_string(clicks) + " times; the dialog did not open again");
882 return checks.result();
883}

885/// @brief Case: no setter calls a handler. Setting a value, replacing options, items or rows, requesting a selection,
886/// opening or closing — none of it is a user's doing, so none of it reaches `onChange`, `onToggle`,
887/// `onSelect`, `onSelectionChange` and the like.
888/// @param probe The backend under test.
889/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
890[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> settersCallNoHandler(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
891 using Options = std::vector<SelectOption>;
892 using std::chrono::milliseconds;
893 reactive::Runtime& runtime = probe.runtime();
894 reactive::Signal<int> phase{runtime, 0};
895 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> rows{runtime, {{.id = 1, .label = "a"}, {.id = 2, .label = "b"}}};
896 std::vector<std::string> fired;
897 auto const note = [&fired](std::string_view handler) {
898 return [&fired, handler](auto const&...) { fired.emplace_back(handler); };
899 };
900 auto const odd = [&phase] { return phase.get() % 2 == 1; };
901 auto const instant = [odd, &phase] {
902 using Instant = std::chrono::sys_time<milliseconds>;
903 return odd() ? std::optional<morph::time::Timestamp>{morph::time::DateTime{Instant{milliseconds{phase.get()}}}}
904 : std::nullopt;
905 };
906 Mounted const view{
907 runtime, probe.backend(),
908 ui::column(
909 {.children = {
910 ui::textInput({.value = [&phase] { return "v" + std::to_string(phase.get()); },
911 .onChange = note("TextInput onChange"),
912 .onSubmit = note("TextInput onSubmit")}),
913 ui::checkbox({.label = "c", .checked = odd, .onToggle = note("Checkbox onToggle")}),
914 // The requested key is 2, then 1; the options hold 2 in odd phases only, so setOptions
915 // re-resolves the request, which is not a user's choice either.
916 ui::select(
917 {.options =
918 [odd] {
919 // Built up by name rather than as two braced lists in a conditional, whose backing
920 // arrays GCC's dangling-pointer analysis mistakes for escaping temporaries.
921 Options options;
922 options.push_back({.key = Key{std::int64_t{1}}, .label = "One"});
923 if (odd()) {
924 options.push_back({.key = Key{std::int64_t{2}}, .label = "Two"});
925 }
926 return options;
927 },
928 .selected = [&phase] { return std::optional<Key>{Key{std::int64_t{phase.get() < 2 ? 2 : 1}}}; },
929 .onSelect = note("Select onSelect")}),
930 ui::menu({.items = {{.label = [&phase] { return "m" + std::to_string(phase.get()); },
931 .onSelect = note("Menu item onSelect")}}}),
932 ui::slider({.value = [&phase] { return std::int64_t{phase.get()}; },
933 .onChange = note("Slider onChange"),
934 .onCommit = note("Slider onCommit")}),
935 ui::dateTimeInput({.value = instant, .onChange = note("DateTimeInput onChange")}),
936 ui::filePicker({.path = [&phase] { return "/p" + std::to_string(phase.get()); },
937 .onPicked = note("FilePicker onPicked")}),
938 ui::panel({.title = "p", .collapsible = true, .collapsed = odd, .onToggle = note("Panel onToggle")}),
939 ui::tabs({.tabs = {{.label = "A", .node = ui::text({.text = "first"})},
940 {.label = "B", .node = ui::text({.text = "second"})}},
941 .selected = [odd] { return odd() ? std::size_t{1} : std::size_t{0}; },
942 .onSelect = note("Tabs onSelect")}),
943 ui::dialog({.open = odd, .title = "d", .onDismiss = note("Dialog onDismiss")}),
944 ui::chart({.data =
945 [&phase] {
946 ChartData data;
947 data.yMax = 4.0;
948 data.summary = "c" + std::to_string(phase.get());
949 return data;
950 }}),
951 entryTable(rows,
952 {.selectionMode = SelectionMode::Multiple,
953 .selection =
954 [&phase] {
955 return phase.get() < 2
956 ? std::vector<Key>{Key{std::int64_t{3}}}
957 : std::vector<Key>{Key{std::int64_t{1}}, Key{std::int64_t{2}}};
958 },
959 .onSelectionChange = note("Table onSelectionChange"),
960 .sort =
961 [odd] {
962 return odd() ? std::optional<TableSort>{TableSort{
963 .column = 0, .direction = SortDirection::Descending}}
964 : std::nullopt;
965 },
966 .onSort = note("Table onSort"),
967 .onActivate = note("Table onActivate")},
968 true),
969 }})};
970 probe.settle();
971 for (int next = 1; next <= 3; ++next) {
972 phase.set(next);
973 // Rows arriving with a requested key, and rows going away, re-mark the table without a user's doing.
974 rows.set(next % 2 == 1 ? std::vector<Entry>{{.id = 2, .label = "b"}, {.id = 3, .label = "c"}}
975 : std::vector<Entry>{{.id = 1, .label = "a"}, {.id = 2, .label = "b"}});
976 probe.settle();
977 }
978 std::string list;
979 for (std::string const& handler : fired) {
980 list += (list.empty() ? "" : ", ") + handler;
981 }
982 Checks checks;
983 checks.that(fired.empty(), "a setter called a handler; only a user's action may: " + list);
984 return checks.result();
985}
986
987/// @brief Case: a Select marks the requested key whenever its options contain it, whichever arrives first, and
988/// remembers the request across options that lack it.
989/// @param probe The backend under test.
990/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
991[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> selectReResolvesRequestedKey(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
992 using Options = std::vector<SelectOption>;
993 SelectOption const one{.key = Key{std::int64_t{1}}, .label = "One"};
994 SelectOption const two{.key = Key{std::int64_t{2}}, .label = "Two"};
995 SelectOption const three{.key = Key{std::int64_t{3}}, .label = "Three"};
996 reactive::Signal<Options> options{probe.runtime(), Options{}};
997 int choices = 0;
998 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
999 ui::select({.options = [&options] { return options.get(); },
1000 .selected = std::optional<Key>{two.key},
1001 .onSelect = [&choices](Key const&) { ++choices; }})};
1002 probe.settle();
1003 Checks checks;
1004 checks.text("a Select whose requested key came before any options", "", probe.textOf(view.root()));
1005 options.set({one, three});
1006 probe.settle();
1007 checks.text("a Select whose options lack the requested key", "", probe.textOf(view.root()));
1008 options.set({one, two});
1009 probe.settle();
1010 checks.text("a Select once options with the requested key arrived", "Two", probe.textOf(view.root()));
1011 options.set({one});
1012 probe.settle();
1013 checks.text("a Select whose new options lack the requested key", "", probe.textOf(view.root()));
1014 options.set({two, one});
1015 probe.settle();
1016 checks.text("a Select whose options bring the requested key back", "Two", probe.textOf(view.root()));
1017 checks.that(choices == 0, "re-marking the requested key called onSelect " + std::to_string(choices) + " times");
1018 return checks.result();
1019}
1020
1021/// @brief Case: a Table in `Multiple` mode reports a user's change as exactly the existing rows now selected.
1022///
1023/// A requested key without a row stays requested through row changes and is marked when its row arrives, and a
1024/// row that goes is unmarked, all without a handler call; a user's change drops the requested keys without a row.
1025/// @param probe The backend under test.
1026/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
1027[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> tableReportsExistingSelectedRows(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
1028 reactive::Runtime& runtime = probe.runtime();
1029 std::vector<Entry> const three{{.id = 1, .label = "a"}, {.id = 2, .label = "b"}, {.id = 3, .label = "c"}};
1030 std::vector<Entry> withNine = three;
1031 withNine.push_back({.id = 9, .label = "i"});
1032 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> rows{runtime, three};
1033 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Key>> selection{runtime, {Key{std::int64_t{2}}, Key{std::int64_t{9}}}};
1034 std::vector<std::vector<Key>> reports;
1035 // The selection is a slot, so the application writes what the user picked for the table to keep showing it.
1036 Mounted const view{runtime, probe.backend(),
1037 entryTable(rows, {.selectionMode = SelectionMode::Multiple,
1038 .selection = [&selection] { return selection.get(); },
1039 .onSelectionChange =
1040 [&reports, &selection](std::vector<Key> keys, SelectionChange) {
1041 reports.push_back(keys);
1042 selection.set(std::move(keys));
1043 }})};
1044 probe.settle();
1045 Checks checks;
1046 checks.text("the rows marked for requested keys 2 and 9, with no row 9", "b", selectedTexts(probe, view.root()));
1047 rows.set(withNine);
1048 probe.settle();
1049 checks.text("the rows marked once row 9 arrived", "b,i", selectedTexts(probe, view.root()));
1050 rows.set(three);
1051 probe.settle();
1052 checks.text("the rows marked once row 9 went", "b", selectedTexts(probe, view.root()));
1053 rows.set(withNine);
1054 probe.settle();
1055 checks.text("the rows marked once row 9 returned", "b,i", selectedTexts(probe, view.root()));
1056 checks.that(reports.empty(), "rows arriving or going called onSelectionChange");
1057 rows.set(three);
1058 probe.settle();
1059 probe.selectRows(view.root(), {0, 2});
1060 probe.settle();
1061 checks.text("the rows marked after the user selected a and c", "a,c", selectedTexts(probe, view.root()));
1062 // A backend may report each step of the user's picking (a click, then a Ctrl-click), so only the last report
1063 // must be the whole selection; but no report may name a key without a row.
1064 bool const rowlessReported = std::ranges::any_of(reports, [](std::vector<Key> const& keys) {
1065 return std::ranges::any_of(keys, [](Key const& key) {
1066 return key != Key{std::int64_t{1}} && key != Key{std::int64_t{2}} && key != Key{std::int64_t{3}};
1067 });
1068 });
1069 std::vector<Key> last = reports.empty() ? std::vector<Key>{} : reports.back();
1070 std::ranges::sort(last);
1071 checks.that(!reports.empty(), "a user's selection of rows 1 and 3 did not call onSelectionChange");
1072 checks.that(!rowlessReported,
1073 "a user's selection, with key 9 requested and no row 9, reported a key without a row");
1074 checks.text("the last report of a user's selection of rows 1 and 3, with key 9 requested and no row 9", "1,3",
1075 keyTexts(last));
1076 rows.set(withNine);
1077 probe.settle();
1078 checks.text("the rows marked once row 9 arrived after the user's selection", "a,c",
1079 selectedTexts(probe, view.root()));
1080 return checks.result();
1081}

1155/// @brief What `LifeSentinel` reports about the handler that holds it.
1156struct HandlerLife {
1157 /// @brief The sentinel inside the handler while that handler runs; null otherwise.
1158 void const* running = nullptr;
1159 /// @brief Set when the running handler's sentinel was destroyed before the handler returned.
1160 bool freedWhileRunning = false;
1161};
1162
1163/// @brief Captured by value in a handler, tells whether the backend destroyed the handler while it ran.
1164///
1165/// Every copy of the handler holds its own sentinel; only the destruction of the copy that is running counts.
1166class LifeSentinel {
1167public:
1168 /// @param life Where to report; must outlive every copy.
1169 explicit LifeSentinel(HandlerLife& life) noexcept : _life{&life} {}
1170
1171 /// @brief Reports its own destruction when it belongs to the running handler.
1172 ~LifeSentinel() {
1173 if (_life->running == this) {
1174 _life->freedWhileRunning = true;
1175 }
1176 }
1177
1178 /// @brief A copy, for another copy of the handler.
1179 LifeSentinel(LifeSentinel const&) = default;
1180 /// @brief Copies the report target.
1181 /// @return This sentinel.
1182 LifeSentinel& operator=(LifeSentinel const&) = default;
1183 /// @brief A copy, for a moved handler.
1184 LifeSentinel(LifeSentinel&&) = default;
1185 /// @brief Copies the report target.
1186 /// @return This sentinel.
1187 LifeSentinel& operator=(LifeSentinel&&) = default;
1188
1189 /// @brief Where it reports.
1190 /// @return The report.
1191 [[nodiscard]] HandlerLife* life() const noexcept { return _life; }
1192
1193private:
1194 HandlerLife* _life;
1195};
1196
1197/// @brief Case: a handler may destroy its own widget; the backend keeps the running handler alive until it returns,
1198/// and stays usable after.
1199/// @param probe The backend under test.
1200/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
1201[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> handlerMayDestroyItsWidget(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
1202 HandlerLife life;
1203 int clicks = 0;
1204 std::optional<Mounted> view;
1205 // After the reset the handler touches nothing it captured: its captures are gone if the backend let them go.
1206 view.emplace(probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
1207 ui::button({.label = "Close", .onClick = [sentinel = LifeSentinel{life}, &view, &clicks] {
1208 HandlerLife* const report = sentinel.life();
1209 std::optional<Mounted>* const own = &view;
1210 ++clicks;
1211 report->running = &sentinel;
1212 own->reset();
1213 report->running = nullptr;
1214 }}));
1215 probe.settle();
1216 probe.click(view->root());
1217 probe.settle();
1218 Checks checks;
1219 checks.that(clicks == 1,
1220 "the click that destroys its own button ran the action " + std::to_string(clicks) + " times");
1221 checks.that(!view.has_value(), "the click did not destroy its own button");
1222 checks.that(!life.freedWhileRunning,
1223 "destroying a button from its own handler destroyed the running handler; the backend must keep it "
1224 "alive until it returns");
1225 Mounted const after{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), ui::text({.text = "after"})};
1226 probe.settle();
1227 checks.text("a Text mounted after a handler destroyed its own widget", "after", probe.textOf(after.root()));
1228 checks.that(clicks == 1, "a handler ran again after it destroyed its own widget");
1229 return checks.result();
1230}

1558 .items = {{.label = "a.txt", .onSelect = choose("a.txt")}}},
1559 {.label = "Delete", .onSelect = choose("Delete"), .enabled = [&deletable] {
1560 return deletable.get();
1561 }}}})};
1562 probe.settle();
1563 probe.chooseMenuEntry(view.root(), {0}); // opens the submenu
1564 probe.chooseMenuEntry(view.root(), {0, 0});
1565 probe.chooseMenuEntry(view.root(), {1}); // disabled
1566 probe.settle();
1567 deletable.set(true);
1568 probe.settle();
1569 probe.chooseMenuEntry(view.root(), {1});
1570 probe.settle();
1571 Checks checks;
1572 checks.that(chosen == std::vector<std::string>{"a.txt", "Delete"},
1573 "choosing a submenu, its entry, a disabled entry and then that entry enabled ran " +
1574 std::to_string(chosen.size()) + " handlers, not the submenu's entry and the enabled one");
1575 return checks.result();
1576}

1761/// @brief Reads where the layout cases' widgets are drawn, and fails a case whose probe reads no geometry.
1762class Geometry {
1763public:
1764 /// @brief Over @p probe.
1765 /// @param probe The backend under test.
1766 /// @param checks The case's checks.
1767 Geometry(ConformanceProbe& probe, Checks& checks) : _probe{&probe}, _checks{&checks} {}
1768
1769 /// @brief Where @p widget is drawn; zero, with the case failed, when the probe reads no geometry.
1770 /// @param widget The widget.
1771 /// @return Its bounds.
1772 [[nodiscard]] WidgetBounds of(Widget const& widget) {
1773 std::optional<WidgetBounds> const bounds = _probe->boundsOf(widget);
1774 _checks->that(bounds.has_value(), "the probe reads no bounds, so a layout case measures nothing");
1775 return bounds.value_or(WidgetBounds{});
1776 }
1777
1778 /// @brief Where @p text draws its lines; zero, with the case failed, when the probe reads none.
1779 /// @param text The text.
1780 /// @return The box around its lines.
1781 [[nodiscard]] WidgetBounds textOf(Widget const& text) {
1782 std::optional<WidgetBounds> const bounds = _probe->textExtentOf(text);
1783 _checks->that(bounds.has_value(), "the probe reads no bounds, so a layout case measures nothing");
1784 return bounds.value_or(WidgetBounds{});
1785 }
1786
1787 /// @brief Checks that a length is what it should be, within one unit.
1788 /// @param what What is measured, for the message.
1789 /// @param expected The length it should be.
1790 /// @param actual The length it is.
1791 void near(std::string_view what, double expected, double actual) {
1792 _checks->that(
1793 actual >= expected - 1.0 && actual <= expected + 1.0,
1794 std::string{what} + ": expected " + std::to_string(expected) + ", got " + std::to_string(actual));
1795 }
1796
1797private:
1798 ConformanceProbe* _probe;
1799 Checks* _checks;
1800};
1801
1802/// @brief A text that sizes as @p layout says.
1803/// @param text The text.
1804/// @param layout Its size request.
1805/// @return The node.
1806[[nodiscard]] inline Node sizedText(std::string text, LayoutHints layout) {
1807 Text made{.text = std::move(text)};
1808 made.common.layout = layout;
1809 return ui::text(std::move(made));
1810}
1811
1812/// @brief @p inner inside a column, so it is sized as a child is: a root fills the window or screen whatever its
1813/// own sizing.
1814/// @param inner The container a case measures.
1815/// @return The column.
1816[[nodiscard]] inline Node insideColumn(Node inner) { return ui::column(Column{.children = {std::move(inner)}}); }
1817
1818/// @brief @p inner inside a row, so its height is sized as a child's is.
1819/// @param inner The container a case measures.
1820/// @return The row.
1821[[nodiscard]] inline Node insideRow(Node inner) { return ui::row(Row{.children = {std::move(inner)}}); }
1822
1823/// @brief The container a case measures, the one child of the mounted root, and its children in order.
1824struct Measured {
1825 /// @brief The measured container; null when the root holds none.
1826 Widget* container = nullptr;
1827 /// @brief Its children.
1828 std::vector<Widget*> children;
1829};
1830
1831/// @brief The container a case measures, inside the root `insideColumn` or `insideRow` made.
1832/// @param probe The backend under test.
1833/// @param view The mount.
1834/// @return It and its children.
1835[[nodiscard]] inline Measured measured(ConformanceProbe& probe, Mounted const& view) {
1836 Measured found;
1837 found.container = probe.childAt(rootContainer(view), 0);
1838 ContainerWidget const* const inner = found.container == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*found.container);
1839 for (std::size_t index = 0; inner != nullptr && index < probe.childCount(*inner); ++index) {
1840 found.children.push_back(probe.childAt(*inner, index));
1841 }
1842 return found;
1843}

1845/// @brief Case: along a row, a stretch child's share stops at its maximum and its stretch sibling takes the rest.
1846/// @param probe The backend under test.
1847/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
1848[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> maximumCapsStretchShare(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
1849 Row row{.children = {sizedText("a", {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .maxWidth = 20}),
1850 sizedText("b", {.width = Sizing::stretch()})}};
1851 row.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(60)};
1852 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::row(std::move(row)))};
1853 probe.settle();
1854 Checks checks;
1855 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
1856 std::vector<Widget*> const children = measured(probe, view).children;
1857 checks.that(children.size() == 2, "the row holds two children");
1858 if (children.size() == 2) {
1859 geometry.near("the capped stretch child's width", 20, geometry.of(*children.at(0)).width);
1860 geometry.near("its stretch sibling's width", 40, geometry.of(*children.at(1)).width);
1861 }
1862 return checks.result();
1863}

1865/// @brief Case: an end-aligned text draws its line at the end of its width, a start-aligned one at the start.

1870 ended.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(20)};
1871 Text started{.text = "abc"};

1934/// @brief The panes of a splitter 41 units wide, which a case measures.
1935/// @param probe The backend under test.
1936/// @param panes The panes' texts and their layout hints.
1937/// @param sizes The splitter's sizes; empty for none.
1938/// @return The mount, to measure the splitter's panes in.
1939[[nodiscard]] inline std::unique_ptr<Mounted> mountedSplitter(
1940 ConformanceProbe& probe, std::vector<std::pair<std::string, LayoutHints>> const& panes, std::vector<int> sizes) {
1941 Splitter split{.children = {}, .orientation = Axis::Horizontal};
1942 for (auto const& [text, hints] : panes) {
1943 split.children.push_back(sizedText(text, hints));
1944 }
1945 split.sizes = Prop<std::vector<int>>{std::move(sizes)};
1946 split.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(41), .height = Sizing::fixed(5)};
1947 auto view =
1948 std::make_unique<Mounted>(probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::splitter(std::move(split))));
1949 probe.settle();
1950 return view;
1951}

1953/// @brief Case: a horizontal splitter without matching sizes places each pane by its own width sizing, and matching
1954/// sizes place them instead.
1955/// @param probe The backend under test.
1956/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
1957[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> splitterPlacesPanesBySizing(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
1958 Checks checks;
1959 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
1960 auto const widthsOf = [&](Mounted const& view) {
1961 std::vector<Widget*> const panes = measured(probe, view).children;
1962 std::vector<double> widths;
1963 widths.reserve(panes.size());
1964 for (Widget const* const pane : panes) {
1965 widths.push_back(geometry.of(*pane).width);
1966 }
1967 return widths;
1968 };
1969 auto const share = mountedSplitter(probe, {{"a", {.width = Sizing::percent(50)}}, {"b", {}}}, {});
1970 std::vector<double> const shares = widthsOf(*share);
1971 checks.that(shares.size() == 2, "the splitter holds two panes");
1972 if (shares.size() == 2) {
1973 geometry.near("a percent(50) pane of a 41-unit splitter", 20, shares.at(0));
1974 geometry.near("the content pane beside it", 20, shares.at(1));
1975 }
1976 auto const equal = mountedSplitter(probe, {{"a", {}}, {"b", {}}}, {});
1977 std::vector<double> const halves = widthsOf(*equal);
1978 checks.that(halves.size() == 2, "the second splitter holds two panes");
1979 if (halves.size() == 2) {
1980 geometry.near("two content panes share equally", halves.at(0), halves.at(1));
1981 }
1982 auto const given = mountedSplitter(probe, {{"a", {.width = Sizing::percent(50)}}, {"b", {}}}, {10, 30});
1983 std::vector<double> const placed = widthsOf(*given);
1984 checks.that(placed.size() == 2, "the third splitter holds two panes");
1985 if (placed.size() == 2) {
1986 geometry.near("a pane placed by matching sizes", 10, placed.at(0));
1987 }
1988 return checks.result();
1989}

2007/// @brief Case: a column's padding insets its children from every edge.
2008/// @param probe The backend under test.
2009/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2010[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> paddingInsetsChildren(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2011 Mounted const view{
2012 probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
2013 insideColumn(ui::column(Column{.children = {sizedText("a", {}), sizedText("b", {})}, .padding = 3}))};
2014 Mounted const bare{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
2015 insideColumn(ui::column(Column{.children = {sizedText("a", {}), sizedText("b", {})}}))};
2016 probe.settle();
2017 Checks checks;
2018 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2019 Measured const padded = measured(probe, view);
2020 Measured const plain = measured(probe, bare);
2021 checks.that(padded.children.size() == 2 && plain.children.size() == 2 && padded.container != nullptr &&
2022 plain.container != nullptr,
2023 "both columns hold two children");
2024 if (padded.children.size() == 2 && plain.children.size() == 2 && padded.container != nullptr &&
2025 plain.container != nullptr) {
2026 WidgetBounds const box = geometry.of(*padded.container);
2027 WidgetBounds const first = geometry.of(*padded.children.at(0));
2028 WidgetBounds const bareBox = geometry.of(*plain.container);
2029 WidgetBounds const bareFirst = geometry.of(*plain.children.at(0));
2030 checks.that(first.x > box.x, "a padded column's child starts inside its left edge");
2031 checks.that(bareFirst.x == bareBox.x, "an unpadded column's child starts at its left edge");
2032 checks.that(bareFirst.y == bareBox.y, "an unpadded column's child starts at its top edge");
2033 checks.that(first.x + first.width < box.x + box.width, "a padded column's child ends inside its right edge");
2034 checks.that(box.height > bareBox.height, "a padded column is taller than the same column unpadded");
2035 }
2036 return checks.result();
2037}

2039/// @brief Case: a two-step padding insets a column's ends and its sides apart.
2040/// @param probe The backend under test.
2041/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2042[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> twoStepPaddingInsetsEndsAndSidesApart(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2043 Mounted const sides{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
2044 insideColumn(ui::column(Column{.children = {sizedText("a", {})}, .padding = Padding{0, 4}}))};
2045 Mounted const ends{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
2046 insideColumn(ui::column(Column{.children = {sizedText("a", {})}, .padding = Padding{4, 0}}))};
2047 probe.settle();
2048 Checks checks;
2049 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2050 Measured const atSides = measured(probe, sides);
2051 Measured const atEnds = measured(probe, ends);
2052 bool const found = atSides.children.size() == 1 && atEnds.children.size() == 1 && atSides.container != nullptr &&
2053 atEnds.container != nullptr;
2054 checks.that(found, "both columns hold one child");
2055 if (found) {
2056 WidgetBounds const sideBox = geometry.of(*atSides.container);
2057 WidgetBounds const sideChild = geometry.of(*atSides.children.at(0));
2058 WidgetBounds const endBox = geometry.of(*atEnds.container);
2059 WidgetBounds const endChild = geometry.of(*atEnds.children.at(0));
2060 checks.that(sideChild.y == sideBox.y, "a column padded [0, 4] starts its child at its top edge");
2061 checks.that(sideChild.x > sideBox.x, "a column padded [0, 4] starts its child inside its left edge");
2062 checks.that(endChild.x == endBox.x, "a column padded [4, 0] starts its child at its left edge");
2063 checks.that(endChild.y > endBox.y, "a column padded [4, 0] starts its child below its top edge");
2064 }
2065 return checks.result();
2066}

2092/// @brief Case: a panel padded by 5 steps whose content is a holder column, the column the interpreter makes for two
2093/// or more nodes, lays a bleeding child from the frame's inner left edge to its inner right edge while its
2094/// sibling stays inside the padding.
2095/// @param probe The backend under test.
2096/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2097[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> bleedingChildOfHeldPanelReachesFrame(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2098 Column holder{.children = {sizedText("bleeds", {.bleed = true}), sizedText("inside", {})}, .holder = true};
2099 Panel panel{.padding = 5, .child = ui::column(std::move(holder))};
2100 panel.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(40)};
2101 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::panel(std::move(panel)))};
2102 probe.settle();
2103 Checks checks;
2104 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2105 Measured const found = measured(probe, view);
2106 ContainerWidget const* const held = found.children.size() == 1 ? asContainer(*found.children.at(0)) : nullptr;
2107 checks.that(found.container != nullptr && held != nullptr && probe.childCount(*held) == 2,
2108 "the panel holds a column of two children");
2109 if (found.container != nullptr && held != nullptr && probe.childCount(*held) == 2) {
2110 WidgetBounds const frame = geometry.of(*found.container);
2111 WidgetBounds const bleeding = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*held, 0));
2112 WidgetBounds const inside = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*held, 1));
2113 // The frame's border is a cell or a pixel or two; the padding is several cells.
2114 checks.that(bleeding.x >= frame.x && bleeding.x - frame.x <= 1.0,
2115 "the bleeding child starts at the frame's inner left edge, not past the padding: it is " +
2116 std::to_string(bleeding.x - frame.x) + " in");
2117 checks.that(frame.width - bleeding.width <= 2.0 + 1e-6 && bleeding.width <= frame.width,
2118 "the bleeding child spans the frame's inner width: " + std::to_string(bleeding.width) + " of " +
2119 std::to_string(frame.width));
2120 checks.that(inside.x - frame.x >= 1.5,
2121 "the sibling stays inside the padding: it is " + std::to_string(inside.x - frame.x) + " in");
2122 }
2123 return checks.result();
2124}

2126/// @brief Case: a tabs node with a page inset of 5 steps whose one page holds a holder column of a bleeding child and
2127/// a sibling lays the bleeding child from the node's left edge to its right edge while the sibling stays
2128/// inside the inset; with the page taller than the tabs node, so that it scrolls, it still does.
2129/// @param probe The backend under test.
2130/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2131[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> bleedingChildOfTabPageReachesNodeEdges(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2132 Checks checks;
2133 for (bool const scrolls : {false, true}) {
2134 std::vector<Node> lines;
2135 lines.push_back(sizedText("bleeds", {.bleed = true}));
2136 for (int line = 0; line < (scrolls ? 12 : 1); ++line) {
2137 lines.push_back(sizedText("inside " + std::to_string(line), {}));
2138 }
2139 Tabs tabs{.tabs = {{.label = "A", .node = ui::column(Column{.children = std::move(lines), .holder = true})}},
2140 .inset = 5,
2141 .pageInset = 5};
2142 tabs.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(40), .height = scrolls ? Sizing::fixed(8) : Sizing::content()};
2143 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::tabs(std::move(tabs)))};
2144 probe.settle();
2145 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2146 Measured const found = measured(probe, view);
2147 ContainerWidget const* const page = found.children.empty() ? nullptr : asContainer(*found.children.at(0));
2148 ContainerWidget const* const held =
2149 page != nullptr && probe.childCount(*page) == 1 ? asContainer(*probe.childAt(*page, 0)) : nullptr;
2150 std::string const where = scrolls ? " (a page that scrolls)" : "";
2151 checks.that(found.container != nullptr && held != nullptr && probe.childCount(*held) >= 2,
2152 "the tabs node holds a page with a column of children" + where);
2153 if (found.container != nullptr && held != nullptr && probe.childCount(*held) >= 2) {
2154 WidgetBounds const node = geometry.of(*found.container);
2155 WidgetBounds const bleeding = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*held, 0));
2156 WidgetBounds const inside = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*held, 1));
2157 geometry.near("the bleeding child's left edge, against the tabs node's" + where, node.x, bleeding.x);
2158 geometry.near("the bleeding child's width, against the tabs node's" + where, node.width, bleeding.width);
2159 checks.that(inside.x - node.x >= 1.5, "the sibling stays inside the page inset" + where + ": it is " +
2160 std::to_string(inside.x - node.x) + " in");
2161 }
2162 }
2163 return checks.result();
2164}

2249/// @brief Case: a column with `justify: end` places its last child's end at its own end, and `between` its first
2250/// child at the start and its last at the end.
2251/// @param probe The backend under test.
2252/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2253[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> columnJustifies(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2254 Checks checks;
2255 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2256 for (Justify const justify : {Justify::End, Justify::Between}) {
2257 Column column{.children = {sizedText("a", {}), sizedText("b", {}), sizedText("c", {})}, .justify = justify};
2258 column.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(20), .height = Sizing::fixed(12)};
2259 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideRow(ui::column(std::move(column)))};
2260 probe.settle();
2261 Measured const inside = measured(probe, view);
2262 checks.that(inside.children.size() == 3, "the column holds three children");
2263 if (inside.children.size() != 3) {
2264 continue;
2265 }
2266 WidgetBounds const outer = geometry.of(*inside.container);
2267 WidgetBounds const first = geometry.of(*inside.children.at(0));
2268 WidgetBounds const last = geometry.of(*inside.children.at(2));
2269 geometry.near(justify == Justify::End ? "end: the last child's end" : "between: the last child's end",
2270 outer.y + outer.height, last.y + last.height);
2271 if (justify == Justify::Between) {
2272 geometry.near("between: the first child's start", outer.y, first.y);
2273 } else {
2274 checks.that(first.y > outer.y + 1, "end: the first child is not at the column's start");
2275 }
2276 }
2277 return checks.result();

2280/// @brief Case: a child capped below its column's width with `alignSelf: center` has equal space either side; a
2281/// stretch child with `maxWidth: 44` in a 70-unit column with `align: center` is 44 wide and centred.
2282/// @param probe The backend under test.
2283/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2284[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> cappedChildCentres(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2285 Checks checks;
2286 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2287 for (bool const own : {true, false}) {
2288 LayoutHints card{.width = Sizing::stretch(), .maxWidth = own ? 20 : 44};
2289 if (own) {
2290 card.alignSelf = Align::Center;
2291 }
2292 Column column{.children = {sizedText("card", card)}, .align = own ? Align::Stretch : Align::Center};
2293 column.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(70)};
2294 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::column(std::move(column)))};
2295 probe.settle();
2296 Measured const inside = measured(probe, view);
2297 checks.that(inside.children.size() == 1, "the column holds one child");
2298 if (inside.children.size() != 1) {
2299 continue;
2300 }
2301 WidgetBounds const outer = geometry.of(*inside.container);
2302 WidgetBounds const placed = geometry.of(*inside.children.at(0));
2303 double const before = placed.x - outer.x;
2304 double const after = (outer.x + outer.width) - (placed.x + placed.width);
2305 geometry.near(own ? "alignSelf center: the capped child's width" : "align center: the card's width",
2306 own ? 20 : 44, placed.width);
2307 geometry.near(own ? "alignSelf center: the space after it, against the space before"
2308 : "align center: the space after the card, against the space before",
2309 before, after);
2310 }
2311 return checks.result();
2312}

2314/// @brief The cells of a table's row, in column order.
2315/// @param probe The backend under test.
2316/// @param table The table.
2317/// @param row The row's position among the table's rows.
2318/// @return Its cells; empty when the table has no such row.
2319[[nodiscard]] inline std::vector<Widget*> rowCells(ConformanceProbe& probe, Widget const& table, std::size_t row) {
2320 std::vector<Widget*> cells;
2321 ContainerWidget const* const rows = asContainer(table);
2322 Widget const* const found = rows == nullptr ? nullptr : probe.childAt(*rows, row);
2323 ContainerWidget const* const inside = found == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*found);
2324 for (std::size_t index = 0; inside != nullptr && index < probe.childCount(*inside); ++index) {
2325 cells.push_back(probe.childAt(*inside, index));
2326 }
2327 return cells;
2328}

2330/// @brief Case: in a 30-unit column with `align: End`, a badge cell ends where the column's text ends: at the
2331/// column's right edge, less the inset a backend gives every cell.
2332/// @param probe The backend under test.
2333/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2334[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> endColumnPlacesBadge(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2335 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> const rows{probe.runtime(),
2336 {{.id = 1, .label = "ok"}, {.id = 2, .label = "x"}}};
2337 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
2338 insideColumn(ui::table<Entry>(
2339 {{.label = "State", .width = Sizing::fixed(30), .align = Align::End}},
2340 [&rows] { return rows.get(); }, [](Entry const& entry) { return Key{entry.id}; },
2341 [](reactive::Signal<Entry> const& entry) {
2342 // Row 1 holds a badge, row 2 a text; both are drawn at the column's end.
2343 Node cell = entry.peek().id == 1
2344 ? ui::badge({.text = [&entry] { return entry.get().label; }})
2345 : ui::text({.text = [&entry] { return entry.get().label; }});
2346 return std::vector<Node>{std::move(cell)};
2347 }))};
2348 probe.settle();
2349 Checks checks;
2350 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2351 Widget const* const table = probe.childAt(rootContainer(view), 0);
2352 std::vector<Widget*> const badgeRow = table == nullptr ? std::vector<Widget*>{} : rowCells(probe, *table, 0);
2353 std::vector<Widget*> const textRow = table == nullptr ? std::vector<Widget*>{} : rowCells(probe, *table, 1);
2354 checks.that(badgeRow.size() == 1 && textRow.size() == 1, "the table holds two rows of one cell");
2355 if (badgeRow.size() == 1 && textRow.size() == 1) {
2356 WidgetBounds const outer = geometry.of(*table);
2357 WidgetBounds const badge = geometry.of(*badgeRow.front());
2358 WidgetBounds const text = geometry.of(*textRow.front());
2359 geometry.near("the badge's right edge, against the column's text's", text.x + text.width,
2360 badge.x + badge.width);
2361 checks.that(badge.x - outer.x > 15, "the badge is not at the end of its 30-unit column: it starts " +
2362 std::to_string(badge.x - outer.x) + " units into the table");
2363 }
2364 return checks.result();
2365}

2442/// @brief Case: in a 5-unit column with `wrap: false`, a text longer than the column is as tall as a text of one

2447 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> const rows{probe.runtime(),
2448 {{.id = 1, .label = "99.4 % LC"}, {.id = 2, .label = "x"}}};
2449 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
2450 insideColumn(ui::table<Entry>(
2451 {{.label = "Assay", .width = Sizing::fixed(5), .wrap = false}},
2452 [&rows] { return rows.get(); }, [](Entry const& entry) { return Key{entry.id}; },
2453 [](reactive::Signal<Entry> const& entry) {
2454 return std::vector<Node>{ui::text({.text = [&entry] { return entry.get().label; }})};
2455 }))};
2456 probe.settle();
2457 Checks checks;

2462 checks.that(longer.size() == 1 && shorter.size() == 1, "the table holds two rows of one cell");
2463 if (longer.size() == 1 && shorter.size() == 1) {
2464 geometry.near("the long text's height, against the short text's", geometry.of(*shorter.front()).height,
2465 geometry.of(*longer.front()).height);
2466 }
2467 return checks.result();
2468}
