2470/// @brief One report of a table's selection: the keys, sorted, and the kind of change.
2471struct SelectionReport {
2472 /// @brief The keys reported, sorted.
2473 std::vector<Key> keys;
2474 /// @brief The kind of change.
2475 SelectionChange change = SelectionChange::Replace;
2476};
2477
2478/// @brief A table over @p rows whose user's selection is recorded in @p reports and shown without a binding.
2479/// @param rows The rows.
2480/// @param mode The selection mode.
2481/// @param reports Where each report goes.
2482/// @param common The table's common properties.
2483/// @return The node.
2484[[nodiscard]] inline Node reportingTable(reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> const& rows, SelectionMode mode,
2485 std::vector<SelectionReport>& reports, Common common = {}) {
2486 return entryTable(rows, {.selectionMode = mode,
2487 .onSelectionChange =
2488 [&reports](std::vector<Key> keys, SelectionChange change) {
2489 std::ranges::sort(keys);
2490 reports.push_back({.keys = std::move(keys), .change = change});
2491 },
2492 .common = std::move(common)});
2493}
2494
2495/// @brief The last report as text: its keys, then `/replace` or `/extend`; `none` when there is none.
2496/// @param reports The reports.
2497/// @return The text.
2498[[nodiscard]] inline std::string lastReport(std::vector<SelectionReport> const& reports) {
2499 if (reports.empty()) {
2500 return "none";
2501 }
2502 return keyTexts(reports.back().keys) +
2503 (reports.back().change == SelectionChange::Replace ? "/replace" : "/extend");
2504}
2505
2506/// @brief Positions as text, comma-separated.
2507/// @param rows The positions.
2508/// @return The text.
2509[[nodiscard]] inline std::string rowTexts(std::vector<std::size_t> const& rows) {
2510 std::string text;
2511 for (std::size_t const row : rows) {
2512 text += (text.empty() ? "" : ",") + std::to_string(row);
2513 }
2514 return text;
2515}
2516
2517/// @brief Rows a, b, c and d, keyed 1 to 4.
2518/// @return The rows.
2519[[nodiscard]] inline std::vector<Entry> fourEntries() {
2520 return {{.id = 1, .label = "a"}, {.id = 2, .label = "b"}, {.id = 3, .label = "c"}, {.id = 4, .label = "d"}};
2521}

2523/// @brief Case: in a `Multiple` table a plain click selects only its row, and a Ctrl-click adds a row and then
2524/// removes it, keeping the first. The click reports `Replace`, each Ctrl-click `Extend`.
2525/// @param probe The backend under test.
2526/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2527[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> clickSelectsCtrlClickToggles(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2528 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> const rows{probe.runtime(), fourEntries()};
2529 std::vector<SelectionReport> reports;
2530 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), reportingTable(rows, SelectionMode::Multiple, reports)};
2531 probe.settle();
2532 Checks checks;
2533 probe.clickRow(view.root(), 2, RowClick::Toggle);
2534 probe.settle();
2535 probe.clickRow(view.root(), 0, RowClick::Only);
2536 probe.settle();
2537 checks.text("the rows selected after a Ctrl-click on c and a click on a", "0",
2538 rowTexts(probe.selectedRows(view.root())));
2539 checks.text("a click's report", "1/replace", lastReport(reports));
2540 probe.clickRow(view.root(), 1, RowClick::Toggle);
2541 probe.settle();
2542 checks.text("the rows selected after a Ctrl-click on b", "0,1", rowTexts(probe.selectedRows(view.root())));
2543 checks.text("a Ctrl-click's report", "1,2/extend", lastReport(reports));
2544 probe.clickRow(view.root(), 1, RowClick::Toggle);
2545 probe.settle();
2546 checks.text("the rows selected after a second Ctrl-click on b", "0", rowTexts(probe.selectedRows(view.root())));
2547 checks.text("the second Ctrl-click's report", "1/extend", lastReport(reports));
2548 return checks.result();
2549}

2551/// @brief Case: a click on row 1, then a Shift-click on row 3, selects rows 1 to 3; a Shift-click on row 0 then

2576/// @brief Case: the keyboard on a focused table of text cells. Ctrl+A on a `Multiple` table selects every row, and
2577/// pressed again clears them, each reported as `Extend`. On a `Single` table Ctrl+A selects nothing and
2578/// reaches the enclosing column's chord, and after a click on row 1, Enter activates row 1.
2579/// @param probe The backend under test.
2580/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2581[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> tableTakesItsKeys(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2582 Checks checks;
2583 {
2584 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> const rows{probe.runtime(), fourEntries()};
2585 std::vector<SelectionReport> reports;
2586 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), reportingTable(rows, SelectionMode::Multiple, reports)};
2587 probe.settle();
2588 probe.press(view.root(), "Ctrl+A");
2589 probe.settle();
2590 checks.text("the rows selected by Ctrl+A on a multiple table", "0,1,2,3",
2591 rowTexts(probe.selectedRows(view.root())));
2592 checks.text("Ctrl+A's report", "1,2,3,4/extend", lastReport(reports));
2593 probe.press(view.root(), "Ctrl+A");
2594 probe.settle();
2595 checks.text("the rows selected by a second Ctrl+A", "", rowTexts(probe.selectedRows(view.root())));
2596 checks.text("the second Ctrl+A's report", "/extend", lastReport(reports));
2597 }
2598 reactive::Signal<std::vector<Entry>> const rows{probe.runtime(), fourEntries()};
2599 std::vector<SelectionReport> reports;
2600 std::vector<Key> activated;
2601 int chords = 0;
2602 Mounted const view{
2603 probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
2604 ui::column({.children = {entryTable(
2605 rows, {.selectionMode = SelectionMode::Single,
2606 .onSelectionChange =
2607 [&reports](std::vector<Key> keys, SelectionChange change) {
2608 reports.push_back({.keys = std::move(keys), .change = change});
2609 },
2610 .onActivate = [&activated](Key const& key) { activated.push_back(key); }})},
2611 .common = {.keys = {{.chord = "Ctrl+A", .onPress = [&chords] { ++chords; }}}}})};
2612 probe.settle();
2613 Widget* const table = childOf(probe, &view.root(), 0);
2614 if (table == nullptr) {
2615 return "a Table in a Column is not shown";
2616 }
2617 probe.press(*table, "Ctrl+A");
2618 probe.settle();
2619 checks.text("the rows selected by Ctrl+A on a single table", "", rowTexts(probe.selectedRows(*table)));
2620 checks.that(chords == 1, "Ctrl+A on a single table ran the column's chord " + std::to_string(chords) + " times");
2621 probe.clickRow(*table, 1, RowClick::Only);
2622 probe.settle();
2623 probe.press(*table, "Enter");
2624 probe.settle();
2625 checks.text("the rows activated by Enter after a click on b", "2", keyTexts(activated));
2626 return checks.result();
2627}

2665/// @brief Case: a click on a sortable column's header reports its index once, a click on another column's header

2699/// @brief Case: in a column of fixed height, a scroll that stretches in height above a text keeps the text at the
2700/// column's end, however long the scroll's content: the scroll takes the column's spare height, not its
2701/// content's.
2702/// @param probe The backend under test.
2703/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2704[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> stretchingScrollKeepsBarAtEnd(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2705 std::vector<Node> lines;
2706 lines.reserve(40);
2707 for (int line = 1; line <= 40; ++line) {
2708 lines.push_back(sizedText("line " + std::to_string(line), {}));
2709 }
2710 Scroll scroll{.child = ui::column(Column{.children = std::move(lines)}), .axis = Axis::Vertical};
2711 scroll.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .height = Sizing::stretch()};
2712 Column column{.children = {ui::scroll(std::move(scroll)), sizedText("bar", {})}};
2713 column.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(30), .height = Sizing::fixed(20)};
2714 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideRow(ui::column(std::move(column)))};
2715 probe.settle();
2716 Checks checks;
2717 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2718 Measured const inside = measured(probe, view);
2719 checks.that(inside.children.size() == 2, "the column holds a scroll and a bar");
2720 if (inside.children.size() == 2) {
2721 WidgetBounds const outer = geometry.of(*inside.container);
2722 WidgetBounds const bar = geometry.of(*inside.children.at(1));
2723 geometry.near("the bar's bottom, at the column's", outer.y + outer.height, bar.y + bar.height);
2724 checks.that(geometry.of(*inside.children.at(0)).height < 20,
2725 "the scroll is as tall as the column or taller, so the bar is pushed out of it");
2726 }
2727 return checks.result();
2728}
2729
2730/// @brief Whether @p inner lies wholly inside @p outer, within half a unit, and is drawn at all.
2731/// @param outer The outer bounds.
2732/// @param inner The inner bounds.
2733/// @return True when it does.
2734[[nodiscard]] inline bool within(WidgetBounds const& outer, WidgetBounds const& inner) {
2735 return inner.height > 0 && inner.y >= outer.y - 0.5 && inner.y + inner.height <= outer.y + outer.height + 0.5;
2736}
2737
2738/// @brief Case: a slot showing a one-row `ForEach`, which is how a switch case is mounted, fills the slot when that
2739/// `ForEach` is sized as the content it holds, a column of a stretching scroll above a bar.
2740/// @param probe The backend under test.
2741/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2742[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> slotShowingStretchingForEachFills(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2743 auto const row = [](reactive::Signal<int> const&) -> Node {
2744 std::vector<Node> lines;
2745 lines.reserve(40);
2746 for (int line = 1; line <= 40; ++line) {
2747 lines.push_back(sizedText("line " + std::to_string(line), {}));
2748 }
2749 Scroll scroll{.child = ui::column(Column{.children = std::move(lines)}), .axis = Axis::Vertical};
2750 scroll.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .height = Sizing::stretch()};
2751 Column held{.children = {ui::scroll(std::move(scroll)), sizedText("bar", {})}};
2752 held.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::content(), .height = Sizing::stretch()};
2753 return ui::column(std::move(held));
2754 };
2755 Common held;
2756 held.layout = {.width = Sizing::content(), .height = Sizing::stretch()};
2757 Switch shown{.selector = [] { return Key{std::int64_t{0}}; },
2758 .cases = {{.key = Key{std::int64_t{0}},
2759 .node = ui::forEach<int>([] { return std::vector<int>{0}; },
2760 [](int const&) { return Key{std::int64_t{0}}; }, row,
2761 Axis::Vertical, 0, held)}}};
2762 shown.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .height = Sizing::stretch()};
2763 Column column{.children = {ui::switchOf(std::move(shown))}};
2764 column.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(30), .height = Sizing::fixed(20)};
2765 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideRow(ui::column(std::move(column)))};
2766 probe.settle();
2767 Checks checks;
2768 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2769 Measured const inside = measured(probe, view);
2770 checks.that(inside.children.size() == 1, "the column holds the switch's slot");
2771 if (inside.children.size() != 1 || inside.children.front() == nullptr) {
2772 return checks.result();
2773 }
2774 // The slot, then the one-row ForEach it shows, then the row it builds, then that row's bar.
2775 Widget const* current = inside.children.front();
2776 for (std::string_view const level : {"the slot", "the one-row ForEach"}) {
2777 ContainerWidget const* const container = current == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*current);
2778 current = container != nullptr && probe.childCount(*container) == 1 ? probe.childAt(*container, 0) : nullptr;
2779 checks.that(current != nullptr, std::string{level} + " holds one child");
2780 }
2781 ContainerWidget const* const content = current == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*current);
2782 if (content == nullptr || probe.childCount(*content) != 2) {
2783 checks.that(false, "the row is a column of a scroll and a bar");
2784 return checks.result();
2785 }
2786 WidgetBounds const outer = geometry.of(*inside.container);
2787 WidgetBounds const bar = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*content, 1));
2788 geometry.near("the bar's bottom, at the column's", outer.y + outer.height, bar.y + bar.height);
2789 return checks.result();
2790}
2791
2792/// @brief A mounted wrapping row and what it holds.
2793struct WrappingRow {
2794 /// @brief The mounted view.
2795 std::unique_ptr<Mounted> view;
2796 /// @brief The row and its children.
2797 Measured measured;
2798};
2799
2800/// @brief Mounts a wrapping row of gap 1 @p width units wide.
2801/// @param probe The backend under test.
2802/// @param width The row's width, in units.
2803/// @param children The row's children.
2804/// @return The row.
2805[[nodiscard]] inline WrappingRow mountWrappingRow(ConformanceProbe& probe, int width, std::vector<Node> children) {
2806 Row row{.children = std::move(children), .gap = 1, .wrap = true};
2807 row.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(width)};
2808 WrappingRow made;
2809 // In a column, which gives a row its natural height; a row would stretch it to the window's.
2810 made.view = std::make_unique<Mounted>(probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
2811 ui::column(Column{.children = {ui::row(std::move(row))}}));
2812 probe.settle();
2813 made.measured = measured(probe, *made.view);
2814 return made;
2815}
2816
2817/// @brief The distance between two fixed(12) texts of a row of gap 1: the backend's own step 1.
2818/// @param probe The backend under test.
2819/// @param geometry Reads bounds.
2820/// @return The distance in units.
2821[[nodiscard]] inline double stepOneDistance(ConformanceProbe& probe, Geometry& geometry) {
2822 Row row{.children = {sizedText("a", {.width = Sizing::fixed(12)}), sizedText("b", {.width = Sizing::fixed(12)})},
2823 .gap = 1};
2824 row.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(40)};
2825 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideRow(ui::row(std::move(row)))};
2826 probe.settle();
2827 Measured const found = measured(probe, view);
2828 if (found.children.size() != 2) {
2829 return 1.0;
2830 }
2831 return geometry.of(*found.children.at(1)).x - geometry.of(*found.children.at(0)).x - 12.0;
2832}
2833
2834/// @brief Case: a wrapping row starts a line only when its next child does not fit.
2835/// @param probe The backend under test.
2836/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2837[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> wrappingRowStartsLineWhenOutOfRoom(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2838 Checks checks;
2839 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2840 double const step = stepOneDistance(probe, geometry);
2841 auto const texts = [] {
2842 std::vector<Node> children;
2843 for (char const* const label : {"one", "two", "three"}) {
2844 children.push_back(sizedText(label, {.width = Sizing::fixed(12)}));
2845 }
2846 return children;
2847 };
2848 {
2849 // Wide enough for all three on a line.
2850 WrappingRow const wide =
2851 mountWrappingRow(probe, static_cast<int>(std::ceil(36.0 + (2.0 * step))) + 1, texts());
2852 checks.that(wide.measured.children.size() == 3, "the wrapping row holds three texts");
2853 if (wide.measured.children.size() == 3) {
2854 double const top = geometry.of(*wide.measured.children.at(0)).y;
2855 geometry.near("the second text's top, on the first's line", top,
2856 geometry.of(*wide.measured.children.at(1)).y);
2857 geometry.near("the third text's top, on the first's line", top,
2858 geometry.of(*wide.measured.children.at(2)).y);
2859 }
2860 }
2861 {
2862 // Room for two: the third starts the next line, under the first.
2863 WrappingRow const narrow = mountWrappingRow(probe, 30, texts());
2864 checks.that(narrow.measured.children.size() == 3, "the narrow wrapping row holds three texts");
2865 if (narrow.measured.children.size() == 3) {
2866 WidgetBounds const row = geometry.of(*narrow.measured.container);
2867 WidgetBounds const first = geometry.of(*narrow.measured.children.at(0));
2868 WidgetBounds const third = geometry.of(*narrow.measured.children.at(2));
2869 geometry.near("the third text's left, at the row's", row.x, third.x);
2870 checks.that(third.y >= first.y + first.height - 0.5, "the third text is below the first line");
2871 geometry.near("the row's height, the two lines'", third.y + third.height - row.y, row.height);
2872 }
2873 }
2874 return checks.result();
2875}
2876
2877/// @brief Case: a stretch child of a wrapping row takes its line's spare width, and its minimum, no more than its
2878/// natural width, is its basis.
2879/// @param probe The backend under test.
2880/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2881[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> wrappingRowStretchTakesLineSpare(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2882 Checks checks;
2883 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2884 double const step = stepOneDistance(probe, geometry);
2885 auto const children = [] {
2886 std::vector<Node> made;
2887 made.push_back(sizedText("a stretch text of well over thirty characters, wider than the row",
2888 {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .minWidth = 10}));
2889 made.push_back(sizedText("fixed", {.width = Sizing::fixed(12)}));
2890 return made;
2891 };
2892 {
2893 WrappingRow const wide = mountWrappingRow(probe, 40, children());
2894 checks.that(wide.measured.children.size() == 2, "the wrapping row holds two texts");
2895 if (wide.measured.children.size() == 2) {
2896 WidgetBounds const stretch = geometry.of(*wide.measured.children.at(0));
2897 WidgetBounds const fixed = geometry.of(*wide.measured.children.at(1));
2898 geometry.near("the stretch text's width, the line less the fixed text and a step", 28.0 - step,
2899 stretch.width);
2900 geometry.near("the fixed text's top, on the stretch text's line", stretch.y, fixed.y);
2901 }
2902 }
2903 {
2904 WrappingRow const narrow = mountWrappingRow(probe, 20, children());
2905 checks.that(narrow.measured.children.size() == 2, "the narrow wrapping row holds two texts");
2906 if (narrow.measured.children.size() == 2) {
2907 WidgetBounds const stretch = geometry.of(*narrow.measured.children.at(0));
2908 WidgetBounds const fixed = geometry.of(*narrow.measured.children.at(1));
2909 geometry.near("the stretch text's width, alone on its line", 20.0, stretch.width);
2910 checks.that(fixed.y >= stretch.y + stretch.height - 0.5, "the fixed text is on the next line");
2911 }
2912 }
2913 {
2914 // A stretch child's minimum is its basis only up to its natural width: a short one with a minimum wider than
2915 // itself leaves the room it would not fill to the child beside it.
2916 std::vector<Node> made;
2917 made.push_back(sizedText("ab", {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .minWidth = 20}));
2918 made.push_back(sizedText("fixed", {.width = Sizing::fixed(12)}));
2919 WrappingRow const row = mountWrappingRow(probe, 30, std::move(made));
2920 checks.that(row.measured.children.size() == 2, "the row of a short stretch text holds two texts");
2921 if (row.measured.children.size() == 2) {

2923 WidgetBounds const fixed = geometry.of(*row.measured.children.at(1));
2924 geometry.near("the fixed text's top, on a short stretch text's line", stretch.y, fixed.y);
2925 }
2926 }
2927 return checks.result();

2930/// @brief Case: a stack told it is the head bar, and then that it is not, keeps its children, their order and their
2931/// visibility.

2934[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> headBarKeepsItsChildren(ConformanceProbe& probe) {

2944 bar->setHeadBar(headBar);

2947 " holds " + std::to_string(probe.childCount(*bar)) +
2948 " children, not 2");
2949 Widget const* const one = probe.childAt(*bar, 0);
2950 Widget const* const two = probe.childAt(*bar, 1);
2951 checks.that(one != nullptr && two != nullptr, "both children are reachable");
2952 if (one != nullptr && two != nullptr) {
2953 checks.text("the first child", "first", probe.textOf(*one));
2954 checks.text("the second child", "second", probe.textOf(*two));

2956 "the first child is shown and the second stays hidden");
2957 }
2958 }

2962/// @brief Case: a scrollable slot of fixed height shows a column of 40 lines inside its own height and brings the
2963/// focused last one into view; holding a column that stretches in height, the column fills it exactly.
2964/// @param probe The backend under test.
2965/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
2966[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> scrollableSlotScrolls(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
2967 Checks checks;
2968 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
2969 IViewBackend& backend = probe.backend();
2970 for (bool const stretching : {false, true}) {
2971 auto const root = backend.createStack(nullptr, Axis::Vertical);
2972 auto const slot = backend.createSlot(root.get());
2973 slot->setLayout({.width = Sizing::fixed(30), .height = Sizing::fixed(20)});
2974 slot->setScrollable(true);
2975 auto const column = backend.createStack(slot.get(), Axis::Vertical);
2976 if (stretching) {
2977 column->setLayout({.width = Sizing::stretch(), .height = Sizing::stretch()});
2978 }
2979 // A button first, so a backend that focuses the first focusable widget on its own focuses the top line, not
2980 // the last.
2981 auto const first = backend.createButton(column.get());
2982 first->setLabel("first");
2983 std::vector<std::unique_ptr<TextWidget>> lines;
2984 for (int line = 2; line < (stretching ? 3 : 40); ++line) {
2985 lines.push_back(backend.createText(column.get()));
2986 lines.back()->setText("line " + std::to_string(line));
2987 }
2988 auto const last = backend.createButton(column.get());
2989 last->setLabel("last");
2990 probe.settle();
2991 WidgetBounds const box = geometry.of(*slot);
2992 geometry.near(stretching ? "the slot's height around a stretching column" : "the slot's height", 20,
2993 box.height);
2994 if (stretching) {
2995 geometry.near("a stretching column's height in the slot", 20, geometry.of(*column).height);
2996 geometry.near("the first line, at the slot's top", box.y, geometry.of(*first).y);
2997 continue;
2998 }
2999 checks.that(!within(box, geometry.of(*last)), "the 40th line lies inside a 20-unit slot before any scroll");
3000 last->focus();
3001 probe.settle();
3002 checks.that(within(box, geometry.of(*last)), "the focused 40th line stays outside the slot");
3003 }
3004 return checks.result();
3005}

3007/// @brief Case: a titled panel of fixed height 20 holding one text keeps the text under its header, not centred; a

3019 auto const text = backend.createText(plain.get());
3020 text->setText("text");

3022 stretched->setTitle("panel");
3023 stretched->setLayout({.width = Sizing::fixed(30), .height = Sizing::fixed(20)});

3042/// @brief Case: a splitter that stretches in a column of fixed height 20 gives each pane the whole 20; a pane that is
3043/// a `pinned` page (a stretching scroll above a bar) keeps its bar at the pane's bottom.
3044/// @param probe The backend under test.

3047 std::vector<Node> lines;

3053 scroll.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .height = Sizing::stretch()};
3054 Column page{.children = {ui::scroll(std::move(scroll)), sizedText("bar", {})}};
3055 page.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .height = Sizing::stretch()};
3056 Splitter split{.children = {ui::column(Column{.children = {sizedText("first", {})}}), ui::column(std::move(page))},
3057 .orientation = Axis::Horizontal};
3058 split.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .height = Sizing::stretch()};

3060 outer.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(40), .height = Sizing::fixed(20)};

3062 probe.settle();

3066 checks.that(inside.children.size() == 1, "the column holds the splitter");
3067 ContainerWidget const* const panes = inside.children.size() == 1 ? asContainer(*inside.children.at(0)) : nullptr;
3068 checks.that(panes != nullptr && probe.childCount(*panes) == 2, "the splitter holds two panes");
3069 if (panes != nullptr && probe.childCount(*panes) == 2) {
3070 WidgetBounds const outerBox = geometry.of(*inside.container);
3071 for (std::size_t index = 0; index < 2; ++index) {
3072 geometry.near("a pane's height", 20, geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*panes, index)).height);
3073 }
3074 ContainerWidget const* const pinnedPane = asContainer(*probe.childAt(*panes, 1));
3075 checks.that(pinnedPane != nullptr && probe.childCount(*pinnedPane) == 2,
3076 "the second pane holds a scroll and a bar");
3077 if (pinnedPane != nullptr && probe.childCount(*pinnedPane) == 2) {
3078 WidgetBounds const bar = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*pinnedPane, 1));
3079 geometry.near("the bar's bottom, at the column's", outerBox.y + outerBox.height, bar.y + bar.height);

3166/// @brief A fixed-width grid of three one-character texts with a least column width, in a column, as mounted by
3167/// `mountMinColumnGrid`.
3168struct MinColumnGrid {
3169 /// @brief The mount, kept alive while the widgets are read.
3170 std::unique_ptr<Mounted> view;
3171 /// @brief The grid's three cells.
3172 std::vector<Widget*> cells;
3173 /// @brief The text after the grid; null when there is none.
3174 Widget* after = nullptr;
3175};
3176
3177/// @brief What `mountMinColumnGrid` mounts.
3178struct MinColumnGridSpec {
3179 /// @brief The grid's width in units.
3180 int width = 0;
3181 /// @brief The grid's least column width in units.
3182 int minColumnWidth = 0;
3183 /// @brief The grid's gap, a spacing step.
3184 int gap = 0;
3185 /// @brief Whether a text follows the grid in the column.
3186 bool withAfter = false;
3187};
3188
3189/// @brief Mounts the grid of `MinColumnGrid`.
3190/// @param probe The backend under test.
3191/// @param spec The grid's width, least column width and gap, and whether a text follows it.
3192/// @return The mount and the widgets read from it.
3193[[nodiscard]] inline MinColumnGrid mountMinColumnGrid(ConformanceProbe& probe, MinColumnGridSpec const& spec) {
3194 Grid grid{.columns = 3, .gap = spec.gap, .minColumnWidth = spec.minColumnWidth};
3195 for (int index = 0; index < 3; ++index) {
3196 grid.cells.push_back(GridCell{.node = sizedText("a", {})});
3197 }
3198 grid.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(spec.width)};
3199 Column column{.children = {ui::grid(std::move(grid))}};
3200 if (spec.withAfter) {
3201 column.children.push_back(sizedText("z", {}));
3202 }
3203 MinColumnGrid made;
3204 made.view =
3205 std::make_unique<Mounted>(probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::column(std::move(column))));
3206 probe.settle();
3207 Measured const found = measured(probe, *made.view);
3208 if (found.children.empty()) {
3209 return made;
3210 }
3211 if (ContainerWidget const* const cells = asContainer(*found.children.at(0)); cells != nullptr) {
3212 for (std::size_t index = 0; index < probe.childCount(*cells); ++index) {
3213 made.cells.push_back(probe.childAt(*cells, index));
3214 }
3215 }
3216 if (spec.withAfter && found.children.size() == 2) {
3217 made.after = found.children.at(1);
3218 }
3219 return made;
3220}

3222/// @brief Case: a grid of three columns with a least column width of 10 units, 25 units wide, shows two columns:
3223/// the third cell starts the second row under the first (25 / 10 is 2).
3224/// @param probe The backend under test.
3225/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3226[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> gridColumnsFollowWidth(ConformanceProbe& probe) {

3233 WidgetBounds const second = geometry.of(*made.cells.at(1));
3234 WidgetBounds const third = geometry.of(*made.cells.at(2));
3235 geometry.near("the third cell's left edge, under the first", first.x, third.x);
3236 checks.that(second.x > first.x + 1.0, "the second cell is in a column of its own");
3237 checks.that(third.y > first.y + 0.5, "the third cell starts the next row");
3238 }
3239 return checks.result();

3318/// @brief Case: a content-sized grid of two columns and no tracks is as wide as its widest cell times its columns:
3319/// for cells of one and ten characters, twice the width the ten characters have on their own (within a unit),
3320/// where the sum of the columns' naturals is about once, and the second cell keeps most of its ten
3321/// characters.
3322/// @param probe The backend under test.
3323/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3324[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> gridColumnsNaturalIsWidestTimesColumns(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3325 Grid grid{.columns = 2};
3326 grid.cells = {GridCell{.node = sizedText("a", {})}, GridCell{.node = sizedText(std::string(10, 'b'), {})}};
3327 grid.common.layout = {.alignSelf = Align::Start};
3328 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::grid(std::move(grid)))};
3329 // The same ten characters on their own: how wide they are in this backend's font, which a character is a unit
3330 // wide of only in a monospace one.
3331 Mounted const alone{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
3332 insideColumn(sizedText(std::string(10, 'b'), {.alignSelf = Align::Start}))};
3333 probe.settle();
3334 Checks checks;
3335 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3336 Measured const found = measured(probe, view);
3337 Widget const* const cell = measured(probe, alone).container;
3338 checks.that(found.container != nullptr && found.children.size() == 2 && cell != nullptr,
3339 "the grid holds two cells");
3340 if (found.container != nullptr && found.children.size() == 2 && cell != nullptr) {
3341 double const width = geometry.of(*found.container).width;
3342 double const natural = geometry.of(*cell).width;
3343 checks.that(natural >= 8, "ten characters are " + std::to_string(natural) + " units wide on their own");
3344 // The columns are as wide as the widest cell, rounded up to a whole pixel at most, so the grid is two of it;
3345 // the sum of the columns' naturals would be about one.
3346 checks.that(width >= (2 * natural) - 0.5 && width <= (2 * natural) + 1,
3347 "the grid is " + std::to_string(width) + " units wide, not twice its ten-character cell (" +
3348 std::to_string(natural) + " units)");
3349 double const second = geometry.of(*found.children.at(1)).width;
3350 checks.that(second >= 8,
3351 "the second cell keeps its ten characters: it is " + std::to_string(second) + " units wide");
3352 }
3353 return checks.result();
3354}

3375/// @brief Case: a badge in a `fixed(12)` track with `align: Center` has as much space before it as after it, within
3376/// a unit.
3377/// @param probe The backend under test.
3378/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3379[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> centredTrackCentresBadge(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3380 Grid grid{.tracks = {GridTrack{.width = Sizing::fixed(12), .align = Align::Center}}};
3381 grid.cells = {GridCell{.node = ui::badge({.text = std::string{"ok"}})}};
3382 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::grid(std::move(grid)))};
3383 probe.settle();
3384 Checks checks;
3385 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3386 Measured const found = measured(probe, view);
3387 checks.that(found.container != nullptr && found.children.size() == 1, "the grid holds one cell");
3388 if (found.container != nullptr && found.children.size() == 1) {
3389 WidgetBounds const outer = geometry.of(*found.container);
3390 WidgetBounds const badge = geometry.of(*found.children.front());
3391 double const before = badge.x - outer.x;
3392 double const after = outer.x + 12 - (badge.x + badge.width);
3393 checks.that(badge.width < 10, "the badge fills its track: it is " + std::to_string(badge.width) +
3394 " units wide, so its track's alignment cannot place it");
3395 geometry.near("the space after the badge, against the space before it", before, after);
3396 }
3397 return checks.result();
3398}

3479/// @brief Case: a segmented select shows its marked option; Right chooses the next one and reports it once, and stops
3480/// at the end; Enter goes on to the enclosing column's chord.
3481/// @param probe The backend under test.
3482/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3483[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> segmentedSelectTakesArrows(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3484 std::vector<Key> chosen;
3485 int chords = 0;
3486 Mounted const view{
3487 probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
3488 ui::column({.children = {ui::select(
3489 {.options = std::vector<SelectOption>{{.key = Key{std::int64_t{1}}, .label = "A"},
3490 {.key = Key{std::int64_t{2}}, .label = "B"},
3491 {.key = Key{std::int64_t{3}}, .label = "C"}},
3492 .selected = std::optional<Key>{Key{std::int64_t{2}}},
3493 .onSelect = [&chosen](Key const& key) { chosen.push_back(key); },
3494 .style = SelectStyle::Segmented})},
3495 .common = {.keys = {{.chord = "Enter", .onPress = [&chords] { ++chords; }}}}})};
3496 probe.settle();
3497 Widget* const select = childOf(probe, &view.root(), 0);
3498 if (select == nullptr) {
3499 return "a segmented Select in a Column is not shown";
3500 }
3501 Checks checks;
3502 checks.text("the marked option", "B", probe.textOf(*select));
3503 probe.press(*select, "Right");
3504 probe.settle();
3505 checks.text("the options chosen by Right", "3", keyTexts(chosen));
3506 probe.press(*select, "Right");
3507 probe.settle();
3508 checks.text("the options chosen by a Right at the end", "3", keyTexts(chosen));
3509 probe.press(*select, "Enter");
3510 probe.settle();
3511 checks.that(chords == 1,
3512 "Enter on a segmented select ran the column's chord " + std::to_string(chords) + " times");
3513 return checks.result();
3514}

3516/// @brief Case: a list entry with content holds it, and a click on the entry or anywhere on its content runs the
3517/// entry's action once; inside a hidden container neither does.
3518/// @param probe The backend under test.
3519/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3520[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> entryContentIsTheEntrys(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3521 reactive::Signal<bool> shown{probe.runtime(), true};
3522 int clicks = 0;
3523 Mounted const view{
3524 probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
3525 ui::column({.children = {ui::button({.label = "WS-2026-0412, 2 h",
3526 .onClick = [&clicks] { ++clicks; },
3527 .style = ButtonStyle::Item,
3528 .child = ui::column({.children = {ui::text({.text = "WS-2026-0412"}),
3529 ui::text({.text = "Assay"})}}),
3530 .selected = true})},
3531 .common = {.visible = [&shown] { return shown.get(); }}})};
3532 probe.settle();
3533 auto* const item = dynamic_cast<ButtonWidget*>(childOf(probe, &view.root(), 0));
3534 if (item == nullptr) {
3535 return "an item button in a Column is not shown";
3536 }
3537 Checks checks;
3538 ContainerWidget const& content = item->content();
3539 checks.that(probe.childCount(content) == 1, "the entry's content holds one column");
3540 auto* const column = dynamic_cast<ContainerWidget*>(probe.childAt(content, 0));
3541 Widget* const first = column != nullptr ? probe.childAt(*column, 0) : nullptr;
3542 if (first == nullptr) {
3543 return "the entry's content shows no text";
3544 }
3545 checks.text("the content's first text", "WS-2026-0412", probe.textOf(*first));
3546 probe.click(*item);
3547 probe.settle();
3548 checks.that(clicks == 1, "a click on the entry ran its action " + std::to_string(clicks) + " times");
3549 probe.click(*first);
3550 probe.settle();
3551 checks.that(clicks == 2, "a click on its content ran the entry's action " + std::to_string(clicks - 1) + " times");
3552 shown.set(false);
3553 probe.settle();
3554 probe.click(*item);
3555 probe.click(*first);
3556 probe.settle();
3557 checks.that(clicks == 2, "a hidden entry took a click");
3558 return checks.result();
3559}

3561/// @brief Case: an open dialog drawn as a sheet fills the surface: a stretching text inside it is as wide as a
3562/// stretching text beside it, less the sheet's own padding, where a centred dialog would be its content's
3563/// width.
3564/// @param probe The backend under test.
3565/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3566[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> sheetFillsSurface(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3567 // What a sheet's border and padding may take off its width, in units; far less than the root is wide.
3568 static constexpr double kSheetPadding = 10;
3569 Column column{.children = {sizedText("beside", {.width = Sizing::stretch()}),
3570 ui::dialog({.open = true,
3571 .title = "Sign",
3572 .child = sizedText("inside", {.width = Sizing::stretch()}),
3573 .onDismiss = {},
3574 .common = {},
3575 .sheet = true})}};
3576 column.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch()};
3577 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), ui::column(std::move(column))};
3578 probe.settle();
3579 Checks checks;
3580 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3581 ContainerWidget const& root = rootContainer(view);
3582 Widget const* const beside = probe.childCount(root) == 2 ? probe.childAt(root, 0) : nullptr;
3583 Widget const* const sheet = probe.childCount(root) == 2 ? probe.childAt(root, 1) : nullptr;
3584 ContainerWidget const* const overlay = sheet == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*sheet);
3585 Widget const* const inside =
3586 overlay != nullptr && probe.childCount(*overlay) > 0 ? probe.childAt(*overlay, 0) : nullptr;
3587 checks.that(beside != nullptr && inside != nullptr, "the root holds a text, and the open sheet holds one");
3588 if (beside != nullptr && inside != nullptr) {
3589 double const full = geometry.of(*beside).width;
3590 double const within = geometry.of(*inside).width;
3591 checks.that(within >= full - kSheetPadding, "a sheet's stretching text is " + std::to_string(within) +
3592 " wide, beside a root " + std::to_string(full) + " wide");
3593 }
3594 return checks.result();
3595}

3653/// @brief Checks that a badge sized by @p sizing is as wide as the same badge sized by its content, and that the
3654/// text after it starts past it.
3655/// @param probe The backend under test.
3656/// @param sizing The badge's width in the narrow row.
3657/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3658[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> badgeRaisedTo(ConformanceProbe& probe, Sizing sizing) {
3659 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
3660 ui::column(Column{.children = {badgeThenText(sizing), badgeThenText(Sizing::content())}})};
3661 probe.settle();
3662 Checks checks;
3663 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3664 Widget const* const narrowWidget = probe.childAt(rootContainer(view), 0);
3665 Widget const* const naturalWidget = probe.childAt(rootContainer(view), 1);
3666 ContainerWidget const* const narrow = narrowWidget == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*narrowWidget);
3667 ContainerWidget const* const natural = naturalWidget == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*naturalWidget);
3668 checks.that(
3669 narrow != nullptr && natural != nullptr && probe.childCount(*narrow) == 2 && probe.childCount(*natural) == 2,
3670 "the column holds two rows of a badge and a text");
3671 if (narrow != nullptr && natural != nullptr && probe.childCount(*narrow) == 2 && probe.childCount(*natural) == 2) {
3672 WidgetBounds const badge = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*narrow, 0));
3673 WidgetBounds const reference = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*natural, 0));
3674 WidgetBounds const after = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*narrow, 1));
3675 geometry.near("the sized badge's width, against its content width", reference.width, badge.width);
3676 checks.that(after.x >= badge.x + badge.width - 1.0,
3677 "the text after the badge starts at " + std::to_string(after.x) +
3678 ", inside the badge, which ends at " + std::to_string(badge.x + badge.width));
3679 }
3680 return checks.result();
3681}

3737/// @brief Whether every condition holds, all of them evaluated: a case reports "the setup is wrong" and skips its
3738/// measurements on one flag, without a short-circuit arm per condition that only a failing backend takes.
3739/// @param conditions The conditions.
3740/// @return True when none is false.
3741[[nodiscard]] inline bool allHold(std::initializer_list<bool> conditions) {
3742 return std::ranges::count(conditions, true) == std::ssize(conditions);
3743}

3745/// @brief Case: a content-sized row of two stretch texts of one and ten characters is as wide as the ten characters
3746/// on their own times its two weights, where the sum of their naturals would be little more than one of
3747/// them, and the ten-character text keeps its characters.
3748/// @param probe The backend under test.
3749/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3750[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> stretchRowNaturalGivesEachItsNatural(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3751 Row row{.children = {sizedText("a", {.width = Sizing::stretch()}),
3752 sizedText(std::string(10, 'b'), {.width = Sizing::stretch()})}};
3753 row.common.layout = {.alignSelf = Align::Start};
3754 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::row(std::move(row)))};
3755 // The same ten characters on their own: how wide they are in this backend's font, which a character is a unit
3756 // wide of only in a monospace one.
3757 Mounted const alone{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
3758 insideColumn(sizedText(std::string(10, 'b'), {.alignSelf = Align::Start}))};
3759 probe.settle();
3760 Checks checks;
3761 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3762 Measured const found = measured(probe, view);
3763 Widget const* const text = measured(probe, alone).container;
3764 bool const ready = allHold({found.container != nullptr, found.children.size() == 2, text != nullptr});
3765 checks.that(ready, "the row holds two texts");
3766 if (ready) {
3767 double const width = geometry.of(*found.container).width;
3768 double const natural = geometry.of(*text).width;
3769 checks.that(natural >= 8, "ten characters are " + std::to_string(natural) + " units wide on their own");
3770 checks.that(width >= (2 * natural) - 0.5 && width <= (2 * natural) + 1,
3771 "the row is " + std::to_string(width) + " units wide, not twice its ten-character text (" +
3772 std::to_string(natural) + " units)");
3773 double const second = geometry.of(*found.children.at(1)).width;
3774 checks.that(second >= natural - 0.5, "the second text keeps its ten characters: it is " +
3775 std::to_string(second) + " units wide, " + std::to_string(natural) +
3776 " on its own");
3777 }
3778 return checks.result();
3779}

3781/// @brief Case: a stretch row nested in a content-sized stretch row keeps its children's naturals: the ten-character
3782/// text in it is as wide as the same characters on their own.
3783/// @param probe The backend under test.
3784/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3785[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> stretchRowNestedKeepsNaturals(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3786 Row inner{.children = {sizedText("a", {.width = Sizing::stretch()}),
3787 sizedText(std::string(10, 'b'), {.width = Sizing::stretch()})}};
3788 inner.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch()};
3789 Row outer{.children = {sizedText("a", {.width = Sizing::stretch()}), ui::row(std::move(inner))}};
3790 outer.common.layout = {.alignSelf = Align::Start};
3791 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::row(std::move(outer)))};
3792 Mounted const alone{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
3793 insideColumn(sizedText(std::string(10, 'b'), {.alignSelf = Align::Start}))};
3794 probe.settle();
3795 Checks checks;
3796 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3797 Measured const found = measured(probe, view);
3798 ContainerWidget const* const nested =
3799 found.children.size() == 2 && found.children.at(1) != nullptr ? asContainer(*found.children.at(1)) : nullptr;
3800 Widget const* const text = measured(probe, alone).container;
3801 std::size_t const nestedCount = nested != nullptr ? probe.childCount(*nested) : 0;
3802 bool const ready = allHold({nestedCount == 2, text != nullptr});
3803 checks.that(ready, "the outer row holds the nested row of two texts");
3804 if (ready) {
3805 double const second = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*nested, 1)).width;
3806 double const natural = geometry.of(*text).width;
3807 checks.that(natural >= 8, "ten characters are " + std::to_string(natural) + " units wide on their own");
3808 checks.that(second >= natural - 0.5,
3809 "the nested ten-character text is " + std::to_string(second) + " units wide, " +
3810 std::to_string(natural) +
3811 " on its own: the nested row asked for less than its children's naturals");
3812 }
3813 return checks.result();

3816/// @brief Case: a stretch child held at its minimum leaves the others to share what is left: three stretch texts in

3821[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> stretchSharesFreezeAtMinimum(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3822 Row row{.children = {sizedText("a", {.width = Sizing::stretch(), .minWidth = 30}),
3823 sizedText("b", {.width = Sizing::stretch()}), sizedText("c", {.width = Sizing::stretch()})}};
3824 row.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(60)};
3825 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(), insideColumn(ui::row(std::move(row)))};
3826 probe.settle();
3827 Checks checks;
3828 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3829 std::vector<Widget*> const children = measured(probe, view).children;
3830 checks.that(children.size() == 3, "the row holds three children");
3831 if (children.size() == 3) {
3832 geometry.near("the child held at its minimum", 30, geometry.of(*children.at(0)).width);
3833 geometry.near("the second child's width", 15, geometry.of(*children.at(1)).width);
3834 geometry.near("the third child's width", 15, geometry.of(*children.at(2)).width);
3835 }
3836 return checks.result();
3837}

3839/// @brief Case: a content-sized spacer in a row shares the spare width as a stretch child of weight 1: beside a

3843[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> spacerCountsAsStretch(ConformanceProbe& probe) {

3858/// @brief Case: two stretch-height children of one and ten lines share a 20-unit column equally.
3859/// @param probe The backend under test.
3860/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3861[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> stretchHeightsShareByWeight(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3862 std::string tall = "l";
3863 for (int line = 1; line < 10; ++line) {
3864 tall += "\nl";
3865 }

3867 .children = {sizedText("l", {.height = Sizing::stretch()}), sizedText(tall, {.height = Sizing::stretch()})}};
3868 column.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::fixed(30), .height = Sizing::fixed(20)};

3870 probe.settle();
3871 Checks checks;
3872 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3873 std::vector<Widget*> const children = measured(probe, view).children;
3874 checks.that(children.size() == 2, "the column holds two children");
3875 if (children.size() == 2) {
3876 geometry.near("the short child's height", 10, geometry.of(*children.at(0)).height);
3877 geometry.near("the tall child's height", 10, geometry.of(*children.at(1)).height);
3878 }
3879 return checks.result();
3880}

3882/// @brief @p lines one-character lines, as one text.
3883/// @param lines How many lines.
3884/// @return The text.
3885[[nodiscard]] inline std::string linesOf(int lines) {
3886 std::string text = "l";
3887 for (int line = 1; line < lines; ++line) {
3888 text += "\nl";
3889 }
3890 return text;
3891}

3893/// @brief Case: two stretch-height children of a panel of fixed height 24, of one and eight lines, share what is left
3894/// under its header equally, whatever their content.
3895/// @param probe The backend under test.
3896/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3897[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> panelStretchHeightsShareByWeight(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3898 Checks checks;
3899 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3900 IViewBackend& backend = probe.backend();
3901 auto const root = backend.createStack(nullptr, Axis::Vertical);
3902 auto const panel = backend.createPanel(root.get());
3903 panel->setTitle("panel");
3904 panel->setLayout({.width = Sizing::fixed(30), .height = Sizing::fixed(24)});
3905 auto const shortText = backend.createText(panel.get());
3906 shortText->setText(linesOf(1));
3907 shortText->setLayout({.height = Sizing::stretch()});
3908 auto const tallText = backend.createText(panel.get());
3909 tallText->setText(linesOf(8));
3910 tallText->setLayout({.height = Sizing::stretch()});
3911 probe.settle();
3912 double const first = geometry.of(*shortText).height;
3913 double const second = geometry.of(*tallText).height;
3914 checks.that(first >= 3 && second >= 3, "the panel's stretch children are " + std::to_string(first) + " and " +
3915 std::to_string(second) + " units tall, where about 10 are left");
3916 geometry.near("the one-line child's height, as tall as its sibling", second, first);
3917 return checks.result();
3918}
3919
3920/// @brief Case: two stretch-height children of an open dialog, of one and eight lines, share the dialog's height
3921/// equally, and the eight-line child keeps its eight lines: the dialog asks for twice the larger natural.
3922/// @param probe The backend under test.
3923/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3924[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> dialogStretchHeightsShareByWeight(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3925 Checks checks;
3926 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3927 IViewBackend& backend = probe.backend();
3928 auto const dialog = backend.createDialog(nullptr);
3929 dialog->setTitle("dialog");
3930 auto const shortText = backend.createText(dialog.get());
3931 shortText->setText(linesOf(1));
3932 shortText->setLayout({.height = Sizing::stretch()});
3933 auto const tallText = backend.createText(dialog.get());
3934 tallText->setText(linesOf(8));
3935 tallText->setLayout({.height = Sizing::stretch()});
3936 dialog->setOpen(true);
3937 probe.settle();
3938 double const first = geometry.of(*shortText).height;
3939 double const second = geometry.of(*tallText).height;
3940 checks.that(second >= 7.5, "the eight-line child is " + std::to_string(second) + " units tall");
3941 geometry.near("the one-line child's height, as tall as its sibling", second, first);
3942 return checks.result();
3943}

3945/// @brief Case: a content-sized panel of two stretch-height children of four lines each, weighted one and two, is
3946/// tall enough for each to keep its four lines: the stretching children ask for `3 * max(4 / 1, 4 / 2)`, where
3947/// the sum of their naturals would squeeze the first to under three lines.
3948/// @param probe The backend under test.
3949/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3950[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> contentSizedPanelKeepsItsStretchChildren(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3951 Checks checks;
3952 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3953 IViewBackend& backend = probe.backend();
3954 auto const root = backend.createStack(nullptr, Axis::Vertical);
3955 auto const panel = backend.createPanel(root.get());
3956 panel->setTitle("panel");
3957 panel->setLayout({.width = Sizing::fixed(30), .alignSelf = Align::Start});
3958 auto const light = backend.createText(panel.get());
3959 light->setText(linesOf(4));
3960 light->setLayout({.height = Sizing::stretch(1)});
3961 auto const heavy = backend.createText(panel.get());
3962 heavy->setText(linesOf(4));
3963 heavy->setLayout({.height = Sizing::stretch(2)});
3964 probe.settle();
3965 double const first = geometry.of(*light).height;
3966 double const second = geometry.of(*heavy).height;
3967 checks.that(first >= 3.5, "the weight-1 child is " + std::to_string(first) + " units tall, its text four");
3968 geometry.near("the weight-2 child's height, twice the first", 2 * first, second);
3969 return checks.result();
3970}

3972/// @brief Case: two stretch-height children of a content-sized scroll area, slot and collapsible, of one and four
3973/// lines, are as tall as each other and the four-line one keeps its four lines: each container asks for twice
3974/// the larger natural, which the equal shares then fill.
3975/// @param probe The backend under test.
3976/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
3977[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> contentContainersShareStretchHeights(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
3978 Checks checks;
3979 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
3980 IViewBackend& backend = probe.backend();
3981 auto const root = backend.createStack(nullptr, Axis::Vertical);
3982 auto const scroll = backend.createScroll(root.get(), Axis::Vertical);
3983 auto const slot = backend.createSlot(root.get());
3984 auto const collapsible = backend.createCollapsible(root.get());
3985 collapsible->setTitle("section");
3986 collapsible->setOpen(true);
3987 std::vector<std::unique_ptr<TextWidget>> texts;
3988 for (ContainerWidget* const container :
3989 {static_cast<ContainerWidget*>(scroll.get()), static_cast<ContainerWidget*>(slot.get()),
3990 static_cast<ContainerWidget*>(collapsible.get())}) {
3991 for (int const lines : {1, 4}) {
3992 texts.push_back(backend.createText(container));
3993 texts.back()->setText(linesOf(lines));
3994 texts.back()->setLayout({.height = Sizing::stretch()});
3995 }
3996 }
3997 probe.settle();
3998 std::array<std::string_view, 3> const names{"scroll", "slot", "collapsible"};
3999 for (std::size_t container = 0; container < names.size(); ++container) {
4000 double const first = geometry.of(*texts.at(2 * container)).height;
4001 double const second = geometry.of(*texts.at((2 * container) + 1)).height;
4002 checks.that(second >= 3.5, "a " + std::string{names.at(container)} + "'s four-line child is " +
4003 std::to_string(second) + " units tall");
4004 geometry.near("a " + std::string{names.at(container)} + "'s one-line child, as tall as its sibling", second,
4005 first);
4006 }
4007 return checks.result();
4008}

4010/// @brief Gives @p container two stretch-height texts of one and four lines, and checks that they are as tall as each
4011/// other once the probe has settled, and that the four-line one keeps its four lines.
4012/// @param probe The backend under test.
4013/// @param container The container to fill.
4014/// @param what What the container is, for the messages.
4015/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
4016[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> checkStretchPair(ConformanceProbe& probe, ContainerWidget& container,
4017 std::string_view what) {
4018 Checks checks;
4019 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
4020 auto const shortText = probe.backend().createText(&container);
4021 shortText->setText(linesOf(1));
4022 shortText->setLayout({.height = Sizing::stretch()});
4023 auto const tallText = probe.backend().createText(&container);
4024 tallText->setText(linesOf(4));
4025 tallText->setLayout({.height = Sizing::stretch()});
4026 probe.settle();
4027 double const first = geometry.of(*shortText).height;
4028 double const second = geometry.of(*tallText).height;
4029 checks.that(second >= 3.5, std::string{what} + "'s four-line child is " + std::to_string(second) + " units tall");
4030 geometry.near(std::string{what} + "'s one-line child, as tall as its sibling", second, first);
4031 return checks.result();
4032}

4034/// @brief Case: two stretch-height children of an open drawer, of one and four lines, are as tall as each other.

4056/// @brief Case: two stretch-height children of a horizontal scroll area of fixed height 20, of one and four lines,
4057/// are as tall as each other.
4058/// @param probe The backend under test.

4060[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> horizontalScrollStretchHeightsShareByWeight(ConformanceProbe& probe) {

4067/// @brief Case: a stretch push button is not narrowed below its label: in a 60-unit row it is as wide as the same
4068/// button sized by its content, and the button beside it gives up the width.
4069/// @param probe The backend under test.
4070/// @return `nullopt`, or what went wrong.
4071[[nodiscard]] inline std::optional<std::string> stretchButtonKeepsItsLabel(ConformanceProbe& probe) {
4072 std::string const label(40, 'b');
4073 auto const buttons = [&label](bool stretch) {
4074 Button shortButton{.label = std::string{"a"}};
4075 Button longButton{.label = label};
4076 if (stretch) {
4077 shortButton.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch()};
4078 longButton.common.layout = {.width = Sizing::stretch()};
4079 }
4080 Row row{.children = {ui::button(std::move(shortButton)), ui::button(std::move(longButton))}};
4081 row.common.layout = stretch ? LayoutHints{.width = Sizing::fixed(60)} : LayoutHints{.alignSelf = Align::Start};
4082 return ui::row(std::move(row));
4083 };
4084 Mounted const view{probe.runtime(), probe.backend(),
4085 ui::column(Column{.children = {buttons(true), buttons(false)}})};
4086 probe.settle();
4087 Checks checks;
4088 Geometry geometry{probe, checks};
4089 Widget const* const sharedWidget = probe.childAt(rootContainer(view), 0);
4090 Widget const* const naturalWidget = probe.childAt(rootContainer(view), 1);
4091 ContainerWidget const* const shared = sharedWidget == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*sharedWidget);
4092 ContainerWidget const* const natural = naturalWidget == nullptr ? nullptr : asContainer(*naturalWidget);
4093 checks.that(
4094 shared != nullptr && natural != nullptr && probe.childCount(*shared) == 2 && probe.childCount(*natural) == 2,
4095 "the column holds two rows of two buttons");
4096 if (shared != nullptr && natural != nullptr && probe.childCount(*shared) == 2 && probe.childCount(*natural) == 2) {
4097 double const wide = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*shared, 1)).width;
4098 double const reference = geometry.of(*probe.childAt(*natural, 1)).width;
4099 checks.that(wide >= reference - 1.0, "the stretch button is " + std::to_string(wide) +
4100 " wide, below its label's " + std::to_string(reference));
4101 }
4102 return checks.result();
4103}

4216/// @brief Every conformance case, in a fixed order.
4217///
4218/// Run each on a fresh probe; `nullopt` is a pass, anything else is the failure message. A backend's test suite
4219/// loops over these with its own `ConformanceProbe`.
4220/// @return The cases.
4221[[nodiscard]] inline std::span<ConformanceCase const> conformanceCases() {
4222 static std::array<ConformanceCase, 56> const cases{{
4223 {.name = "a Text shows its constant text", .run = detail::textShowsItsText},
4224 {.name = "a bound Text updates once per batch and not for an equal write",
4225 .run = detail::boundTextUpdatesOncePerChange},
4226 {.name = "visible and enabled follow their bindings", .run = detail::visibleAndEnabledFollowBindings},
4227 {.name = "a click runs the button's action once", .run = detail::clickReachesAction},
4228 {.name = "typing reaches onChange and a value set by the application is not echoed",
4229 .run = detail::typingWithoutEcho},
4230 {.name = "a Switch shows the selected case and nothing for a key without one",
4231 .run = detail::switchShowsSelectedCase},
4232 {.name = "Tabs mount a page on first selection and show only the selected one",
4233 .run = detail::tabsMountPagesLazily},
4234 {.name = "a ForEach updates a kept row in place", .run = detail::forEachUpdatesInPlace},
4235 {.name = "a ForEach follows inserts, removals and reorders", .run = detail::forEachInsertsRemovesReorders},
4236 {.name = "a moved widget keeps its native state", .run = detail::movedRowKeepsNativeState},
4237 {.name = "a Dialog holds its content only while open", .run = detail::dialogHoldsContentWhileOpen},
4238 {.name = "a new Dialog is closed and a closed Dialog takes no input", .run = detail::closedDialogTakesNoInput},
4239 {.name = "a widget inside a hidden, disabled or collapsed container takes no input",
4240 .run = detail::unreachableWidgetsTakeNoInput},
4241 {.name = "a setter given the text a field shows keeps the cursor", .run = detail::unchangedTextKeepsCursor},
4242 {.name = "a text field shows what the document makes of an edit", .run = detail::textInputIsControlled},
4243 {.name = "a dismissal the document refuses leaves the dialog open",
4244 .run = detail::refusedDismissalKeepsDialogOpen},
